Grammar is the system of rules used to organize words into sentences.
English grammar describes how words are combined to communicate meaning.
A sentence normally contains a subject and a predicate.
A subject is the person, place, thing, or idea performing an action or being described.
A predicate tells what the subject does or what happens to the subject.
A noun is a word that represents a person, place, thing, or idea.
A proper noun is the specific name of a person, place, organization, or thing.
A common noun refers to a general person, place, thing, or idea.
A pronoun is a word that can replace a noun.
Personal pronouns include words such as I, you, he, she, it, we, and they.
A verb is a word that expresses an action, occurrence, or state of being.
An action verb describes an action performed by a subject.
A linking verb connects a subject with additional information about the subject.
The verb "to be" is commonly used as a linking verb.
An adjective describes or modifies a noun or pronoun.
An adverb can modify a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
A preposition shows a relationship between words.
Common prepositions include in, on, at, under, over, beside, and between.
A conjunction connects words, phrases, or clauses.
A coordinating conjunction connects grammatical elements of similar importance.
The coordinating conjunctions are for, and, nor, but, or, yet, and so.
A subordinating conjunction introduces a dependent clause.
An interjection expresses a sudden emotion or reaction.
An article is a word placed before a noun.
The English indefinite articles are "a" and "an."
The English definite article is "the."
A singular noun refers to one person, place, thing, or idea.
A plural noun refers to more than one person, place, thing, or idea.

Many English plural nouns are formed by adding "s."
Some plural nouns are formed by adding "es."
Some English nouns have irregular plural forms.
The plural of "child" is "children."
The plural of "mouse" is "mice."
The plural of "person" can be "people."
The plural of "tooth" is "teeth."
The plural of "foot" is "feet."
A possessive noun shows ownership or association.
An apostrophe and "s" can be used to show possession.
The phrase "the student's book" shows that the book belongs to the student.

A plural possessive noun ending in "s" usually takes an apostrophe after the "s."
The phrase "the students' books" shows that the books belong to multiple students.
The subject of a sentence performs the action of an action verb.
The object of a sentence receives the action of a transitive verb.
In the sentence "The dog chased the ball," the dog is the subject.
In the sentence "The dog chased the ball," the ball is the direct object.
A direct object directly receives the action of a verb.
An indirect object identifies who or what receives something.
A sentence fragment is an incomplete sentence.
A sentence fragment may be missing a subject or a predicate.
A complete sentence expresses a complete thought.
A run-on sentence incorrectly combines two or more independent clauses.
A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are incorrectly joined with a comma.
A sentence can be corrected by separating independent clauses with a period.
A semicolon can join closely related independent clauses.
A coordinating conjunction can join independent clauses when used with a comma.
An independent clause can stand alone as a complete sentence.
A dependent clause cannot normally stand alone as a complete sentence.
A dependent clause often begins with a subordinating conjunction.
A complex sentence contains an independent clause and at least one dependent clause.
A compound sentence contains at least two independent clauses.
A compound-complex sentence contains multiple independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
A simple sentence contains one independent clause.
A simple sentence can still contain multiple subjects or verbs.
A declarative sentence makes a statement.
An interrogative sentence asks a question.
An imperative sentence gives a command or instruction.
An exclamatory sentence expresses strong emotion.
A question usually ends with a question mark.
A strong exclamation usually ends with an exclamation mark.
A normal statement usually ends with a period.
Verb tense indicates when an action or state occurs.
The present tense commonly describes actions or states happening now or regularly.
The past tense commonly describes actions or states that occurred previously.
The future tense describes actions or states that are expected to occur later.
The present progressive describes an action that is currently happening.
The past progressive describes an ongoing action that occurred in the past.
The present perfect connects a past action or event with the present.
The past perfect describes an action that happened before another past event.
The future perfect describes an action that will be completed before a future point.
Regular English verbs commonly form the simple past by adding "-ed."
Irregular verbs do not follow the standard "-ed" pattern.
The past tense of "walk" is "walked."
The past tense of "go" is "went."
The past tense of "eat" is "ate."
The past tense of "write" is "wrote."
The past tense of "see" is "saw."
The past tense of "run" is "ran."
Subject-verb agreement means that the subject and verb must agree in number.
A singular subject generally takes a singular verb in the present tense.
A plural subject generally takes a plural verb in the present tense.
The sentence "She runs every morning" has subject-verb agreement.
The sentence "They run every morning" has subject-verb agreement.
"The dogs bark" is grammatically consistent with plural subject-verb agreement.
"The dog barks" is grammatically consistent with singular subject-verb agreement.
An adjective can describe the size, color, age, or quality of a noun.
In the phrase "the red car," the word "red" is an adjective.
A comparative adjective compares two things.
A superlative adjective compares three or more things.
"Faster" is a comparative form of "fast."
"Fastest" is a superlative form of "fast."
"Better" is the comparative form of "good."
"Best" is the superlative form of "good."
An adverb can describe how, when, where, or to what extent something happens.
Many adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to an adjective.
In the sentence "She ran quickly," the word "quickly" is an adverb.
An adverb can modify a verb.
An adverb can also modify an adjective.
In the phrase "very cold," the word "very" modifies the adjective "cold."
A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition and includes its object.
In the phrase "under the table," the word "under" is a preposition.
The phrase "under the table" is a prepositional phrase.
Prepositional phrases can provide information about location.
Prepositional phrases can also provide information about time, direction, or relationships.
A conjunction can connect two words.
A conjunction can connect two phrases.
A conjunction can connect two clauses.
"And" commonly adds related information.
"But" commonly introduces contrast.
"Or" commonly presents alternatives.
"Because" commonly introduces a reason.
"Although" commonly introduces a contrast or concession.
Capitalization is the use of uppercase letters in appropriate places.
The first word of a sentence is normally capitalized.
Proper nouns normally begin with capital letters.
The pronoun "I" is always capitalized in English.
Days of the week are capitalized.
Months of the year are capitalized.
Languages and nationalities are capitalized.
The word "english" should normally be written as "English."
The word "canada" should normally be written as "Canada."
Punctuation helps organize and clarify written language.
A period normally ends a declarative sentence.
A question mark normally ends a direct question.
An exclamation mark indicates strong emotion or emphasis.
A comma can separate items in a list.
A comma can separate certain introductory elements.
A semicolon can connect closely related independent clauses.
A colon can introduce a list or explanation.
Quotation marks can indicate direct speech or quoted material.
An apostrophe can indicate possession or contraction.
A hyphen can connect certain compound words.
A contraction combines two words into a shorter form.
"Do not" can be contracted to "don't."
"Cannot" can be contracted to "can't."
"They are" can be contracted to "they're."
"She is" can be contracted to "she's."
"It is" can be contracted to "it's."
"Who is" can be contracted to "who's."
"Whose" is a possessive word and is different from "who's."
"Your" is a possessive determiner.
"You're" is a contraction of "you are."
"Your" and "you're" have different grammatical functions.
"To" can function as a preposition or part of an infinitive.
"Too" can mean excessively or additionally.
"Two" is the number 2.
"Their" is a possessive determiner.
"They're" is a contraction of "they are."
"There" commonly refers to a place or introduces an expression.
"Their," "they're," and "there" are commonly confused words.
"Then" commonly refers to time or sequence.
"Than" is commonly used when comparing things.
"Affect" is commonly used as a verb meaning to influence.
"Effect" is commonly used as a noun meaning a result.
"Accept" means to receive or agree to something.
"Except" means excluding something.
"Advice" is a noun.
"Advise" is a verb.
"Principal" can refer to a person in charge of a school.
"Principle" means a fundamental rule, belief, or idea.
A metaphor compares two things without using "like" or "as."
The sentence "Time is a thief" contains a metaphor.
A simile compares two things using words such as "like" or "as."
The sentence "He runs like the wind" contains a simile.
Personification gives human characteristics to nonhuman things.
The phrase "the wind whispered" is an example of personification.
Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis.
The phrase "I have told you a million times" is an example of hyperbole.
quotes: I have told you a million times

sentences.text: Onomatopoeia uses words that imitate sounds.
Words such as "buzz," "bang," and "hiss" are examples of onomatopoeia.
Alliteration repeats similar beginning sounds in nearby words.
The phrase "Peter Piper picked" contains alliteration.
Assonance involves repeated vowel sounds.
Consonance involves repeated consonant sounds.
A theme is a central idea explored in a literary work.
A plot is the sequence of events in a story.
A character is a person, animal, or other figure in a story.
The protagonist is generally the central character of a story.
The antagonist is a character or force that opposes the protagonist.
The setting describes where and when a story takes place.
Conflict is a struggle between opposing forces.
Internal conflict occurs within a character.
External conflict occurs between a character and an outside force.
The climax is a major turning point in a story.
The resolution is the part of a story in which major conflicts are resolved.
First-person point of view uses pronouns such as "I" and "we."
Second-person point of view commonly uses the pronoun "you."
Third-person point of view uses pronouns such as "he," "she," and "they."
A first-person narrator is a character who tells the story from their perspective.
An omniscient narrator can provide information about multiple characters.
A limited third-person narrator generally follows the perspective of one character.
A thesis statement presents the central argument or claim of an essay.
A topic sentence introduces the main idea of a paragraph.
Supporting evidence provides information that supports an argument.
A conclusion summarizes or reinforces the main ideas of an essay.
A paragraph normally develops one main idea.
A transition connects ideas between sentences or paragraphs.
An introduction normally presents the topic and purpose of an essay.
An argumentative essay presents a claim supported by reasoning and evidence.
A persuasive essay attempts to convince the reader of a position.
An expository essay explains or informs the reader about a topic.
A narrative essay tells a story or describes an experience.
A descriptive essay uses details to create a vivid impression.
A literary analysis examines elements and techniques used in literature.
A claim is a statement that can be supported with evidence.
Evidence is information used to support a claim.
Reasoning explains how evidence supports a claim.
A counterargument presents an opposing position.
A rebuttal responds to or challenges a counterargument.
Credibility refers to the trustworthiness of a source or argument.
Logical reasoning connects evidence and conclusions in a rational way.
Plagiarism is presenting someone else's work or ideas as one's own.

sentences.text: A quotation directly uses words from another source.
A paraphrase restates information using different wording.
A summary gives a shorter version of the main ideas.
A citation identifies the source of information.
Academic writing normally requires appropriate attribution of sources.
A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning or spelling.
"To," "too," and "two" are examples of commonly confused homophones.
"Sea" and "see" are homophones.
"Right" and "write" are homophones.
"Flower" and "flour" are homophones.
A synonym is a word with a similar meaning to another word.
"Happy" and "joyful" can be synonyms.
An antonym is a word with an opposite meaning.
"Hot" and "cold" are antonyms.
A word's meaning can depend on its context.
Context provides information that helps determine the meaning of a word.
A prefix is added to the beginning of a word.
A suffix is added to the end of a word.
The prefix "un-" can indicate negation.
The suffix "-less" can indicate the absence of something.
The suffix "-ful" can indicate that something is characterized by or full of something.
A root word is a basic form from which other words can be created.
Word roots can help readers determine unfamiliar word meanings.
A clause is a group of words containing a subject and a verb.
A phrase is a group of words that functions as a unit but does not normally contain both a subject and a predicate.
A noun phrase is a phrase centered around a noun.
A verb phrase contains a main verb and any helping verbs.
An infinitive is commonly formed with "to" followed by the base form of a verb.
"To run" is an example of an infinitive.
A gerund is an "-ing" form of a verb functioning as a noun.
In the sentence "Swimming is fun," "swimming" functions as a gerund.
A helping verb works with a main verb.
Common helping verbs include forms of "be," "have," and "do."
Modal verbs express possibility, ability, permission, necessity, or obligation.
Common modal verbs include can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, and would.
"Can" can express ability.
"Must" can express necessity.
"Should" can express advice or expectation.
Active voice emphasizes the subject performing an action.
Passive voice emphasizes the recipient of an action.
"The scientist conducted the experiment" is written in active voice.
"The experiment was conducted by the scientist" is written in passive voice.
quotes: The experiment was conducted by the scientist

sentences.text: Passive voice is formed using a form of "be" and a past participle.
A dangling modifier is a modifier that does not clearly modify the intended word.
A misplaced modifier is positioned so that its meaning is unclear or misleading.
Clear sentence structure helps prevent modifier errors.
Parallel structure means using grammatically similar structures in related elements.
Parallel structure improves clarity and readability.
A double negative occurs when two negative elements are used in a way that can create unintended meaning.
Standard English grammar generally avoids certain double-negative constructions.
Informal speech may use grammatical patterns that differ from formal writing.
Formal writing generally follows standardized grammar and punctuation conventions.
Grammar can vary between dialects and varieties of English.
British English and American English have some differences in spelling and vocabulary.
"Colour" is a common British English spelling.
"Color" is a common American English spelling.
"Centre" is a common British English spelling.
"Center" is a common American English spelling.
British English and American English use many of the same grammatical structures.
Canadian English contains features associated with both British and American English.
English has many regional dialects and varieties.
Reading comprehension involves understanding and interpreting written information.
The main idea is the central point of a passage.
A supporting detail provides information related to the main idea.
An inference is a conclusion drawn from available information.
Context clues can help readers determine unfamiliar word meanings.
Summarizing involves identifying and restating the most important information.
Analyzing a text involves examining its ideas, structure, language, and evidence.
Evaluating a source involves considering its reliability, evidence, purpose, and credibility.
A literary symbol is an object, character, place, or idea that represents a deeper meaning.
Foreshadowing provides clues about events that may occur later.
Irony occurs when there is a contrast between expectation and reality.
Dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows information that a character does not know.
Situational irony occurs when the outcome differs from what is expected.
Verbal irony occurs when a speaker's intended meaning differs from the literal wording.
A sonnet is a poem traditionally consisting of fourteen lines.
A stanza is a grouped section of lines in a poem.
Rhyme occurs when words have matching or similar sounds.
A rhyme scheme describes the pattern of rhymes in a poem.
Meter refers to the rhythmic structure of a poem.
Free verse does not follow a consistent traditional meter or rhyme scheme.
Imagery uses descriptive language to create sensory impressions.

Metalworking is the process of shaping, cutting, joining, or modifying metal.
Metalworking includes machining, welding, casting, forging, forming, and fabrication.
Metal fabrication involves creating structures or components from metal.
A metalworker may use hand tools, power tools, machines, or industrial equipment.
Different metals require different tools, cutting speeds, temperatures, and techniques.
Steel is an alloy primarily composed of iron and carbon.
Carbon steel contains carbon as its main alloying element.
Stainless steel contains enough chromium to provide significant corrosion resistance.
Aluminum is a lightweight metal commonly used in fabrication and machining.
Copper is a highly conductive metal commonly used in electrical applications.
Brass is an alloy primarily composed of copper and zinc.
Bronze is generally an alloy primarily composed of copper and tin.
Cast iron contains a relatively high amount of carbon.
Titanium is a strong and lightweight metal with excellent corrosion resistance.
A vise is used to hold a workpiece securely.
A bench vise is commonly mounted to a workbench.
Soft jaws can protect a workpiece from damage while it is held in a vise.
Clamps are used to temporarily hold workpieces together.
Locking pliers can clamp and hold metal components.
A C-clamp is a common tool for securing metal workpieces.
A hacksaw is a hand tool used to cut metal.
A hacksaw uses a replaceable toothed blade.

A file is a hand tool used to remove small amounts of material.
A flat file is useful for smoothing flat surfaces.
A round file is useful for working on curved or round openings.
A half-round file has both flat and curved surfaces.
A deburring tool removes sharp edges and burrs from machined parts.
An angle grinder is a handheld power tool used for cutting, grinding, and polishing.
An abrasive cutting wheel can be used to cut metal.
A grinding wheel can remove material from a metal workpiece.
A flap disc can be used for grinding and surface finishing.
A wire wheel can remove rust, paint, and surface contamination.
An angle grinder can generate sparks and significant heat.
A drill press is a machine used to drill accurate holes.
A handheld drill can be used for portable drilling operations.
A drill bit is a cutting tool used to create holes.
A twist drill is one of the most common types of drill bit.
High-speed steel drill bits are commonly used for metalworking.
Cobalt drill bits can provide increased heat resistance.
A center punch creates a small indentation before drilling.
A pilot hole can help guide a larger drill bit.
A countersink creates a conical recess around a hole.
A counterbore creates a cylindrical recess around a hole.
A reamer is used to accurately finish an existing hole.
A tap cuts internal threads inside a hole.
A die cuts external threads onto a cylindrical workpiece.
Tapping fluid can help lubricate and cool a tap during threading.
A lathe is a machine that rotates a workpiece while a cutting tool removes material.
A metalworking lathe can produce cylindrical components.
Turning is a lathe operation that reduces the diameter of a workpiece.
Facing is a lathe operation that creates a flat end surface.
Parting is a lathe operation used to cut a workpiece off.
Threading on a lathe creates threads on a cylindrical workpiece.
Knurling creates a textured pattern on a cylindrical surface.
A chuck holds a workpiece in a lathe.
A three-jaw chuck automatically centers many round workpieces.
A four-jaw chuck can independently adjust each jaw.
A tailstock supports the end of a long workpiece.
A cutting tool is used to remove material from a rotating workpiece.
A milling machine removes material using a rotating cutting tool.
A mill can create slots, flats, pockets, and complex shapes.
An end mill is a common milling cutter.
A face mill is used to machine large flat surfaces.
A vise can hold a workpiece on a milling machine.
A vertical milling machine has a spindle oriented vertically.
A horizontal milling machine has a spindle oriented horizontally.
CNC milling machines use computer-controlled movements.
CNC stands for computer numerical control.
A CNC machine follows programmed instructions to control its movements.
CNC machining can produce highly repeatable components.
G-code is commonly used to control CNC machines.
A CNC router can cut materials using a rotating cutting tool.
A CNC mill is designed for precision machining.
A CNC lathe can automatically perform turning operations.
Computer-aided manufacturing software can generate machining toolpaths.
A cutting speed describes how quickly the cutting surface moves relative to the workpiece.
Feed rate describes how quickly the cutting tool moves through the material.
Depth of cut describes how deeply a cutting tool removes material.
Cutting parameters affect tool life, surface finish, and machining time.
Using an excessive cutting speed can generate excessive heat.
Using an excessive feed rate can overload a cutting tool.
Coolant can reduce heat and friction during machining.
Cutting fluid can improve tool life and surface finish.
A burr is a small unwanted ridge of material left after cutting or machining.
Deburring removes unwanted sharp edges and burrs.
A chamfer is an angled edge added to a workpiece.
A radius is a curved transition between surfaces.
A fillet is a rounded internal corner.
A sharp edge can be dangerous and may require deburring.
Welding is a process used to permanently join materials.
Arc welding uses an electric arc to generate heat.
MIG welding uses a continuously fed wire electrode.
MIG stands for metal inert gas.
MIG welding is commonly used for steel, stainless steel, and aluminum.
TIG welding uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode.
TIG stands for tungsten inert gas.
TIG welding can produce precise and clean welds.
Stick welding uses a consumable flux-coated electrode.
Stick welding is commonly used for steel and outdoor fabrication.
A welding electrode conducts current and may provide filler metal.
A welding torch directs heat toward the workpiece.
A welding gun is commonly used for MIG welding.
Shielding gas protects the weld area from atmospheric contamination.
Argon is commonly used as a shielding gas for TIG welding.
Carbon dioxide can be used as a shielding gas in some MIG applications.
An inert gas does not readily react with other substances.
Flux helps protect certain welding operations from contamination.
A weld bead is the visible deposited metal produced by welding.
A fillet weld joins two surfaces that meet at an angle.
A butt weld joins two pieces along their edges.
A groove weld is made in a groove between workpieces.
A tack weld temporarily holds parts in position.
Welding penetration describes how deeply the weld fuses into the base material.
A weld joint is the region where two pieces are joined.
Heat-affected zone refers to material near a weld that has been altered by heat.
Porosity is a welding defect involving gas pockets in the weld.
Undercut is a groove melted into the base metal beside a weld.
Cracking is a serious welding defect that can weaken a joint.
Lack of fusion occurs when weld metal does not properly fuse with the base material.
Lack of penetration occurs when the weld does not penetrate sufficiently into the joint.
Welding defects can result from contamination, incorrect settings, poor technique, or improper preparation.
Welding helmets protect the eyes and face from welding radiation and sparks.
Welding gloves protect the hands from heat and sparks.
A welding jacket or protective clothing can reduce exposure to sparks and heat.
Safety glasses protect the eyes from flying particles.
Hearing protection can reduce exposure to loud machinery.
Respiratory protection may be required for certain hazardous fumes.
Proper ventilation helps reduce exposure to welding fumes.
Arc welding produces ultraviolet radiation.
Ultraviolet radiation from welding can cause serious eye and skin injuries.
Arc eye is a painful eye injury caused by excessive exposure to welding radiation.
Welding fumes can contain hazardous substances.
Metalworking areas should have appropriate ventilation.
Flammable materials should be kept away from sparks and hot metal.
Forging shapes metal using compressive forces.
Forging can be performed while metal is hot or cold.
Hot forging heats metal until it becomes easier to deform.
A forge is an apparatus used to heat metal.
An anvil provides a solid surface for forging.
A hammer can deliver impact forces during forging.
A power hammer mechanically delivers repeated forging blows.
Forging can produce strong components because of changes in the metal's structure and grain flow.

A foundry is a facility where metal casting is performed.
Sand casting uses sand to create a mold.
Investment casting uses a detailed expendable mold.
Die casting forces molten metal into a reusable metal mold.
Casting is useful for producing complex shapes.
A furnace is used to heat metal to high temperatures.
A crucible is a container designed to hold molten metal.
Molten metal is metal that has been heated above its melting point.
A sprue is a passage through which molten metal enters a mold.
A riser supplies additional molten metal as a casting solidifies.

A shear is a machine used to cut sheet metal.
A brake is a machine used to bend sheet metal.
A press brake uses a punch and die to bend sheet metal.
A slip roll forms sheet metal into curved shapes.
A metal shear can produce straight cuts in sheet material.
A nibbler removes small sections of sheet metal to create cuts.
A punch press uses a punch and die to cut or form sheet metal.
Punching creates holes by forcing a punch through sheet material.
Stamping uses dies to form or cut sheet metal.
Deep drawing forms sheet metal into deeper shapes.
Sheet metal thickness is commonly specified using gauges or direct thickness measurements.
Heat treatment changes the properties of metal through controlled heating and cooling.
Annealing generally softens metal and can reduce internal stresses.
Normalizing can refine the structure of certain steels.
Hardening can increase the hardness of steel.
Quenching rapidly cools heated metal.
Tempering reduces some of the brittleness produced by hardening.
Heat treatment must use appropriate temperatures and cooling methods for the specific alloy.
Hardness describes a material's resistance to indentation or deformation.
Tensile strength describes the maximum stress a material can withstand while being stretched.
Yield strength is the stress at which significant permanent deformation begins.
Ductility describes how much a material can deform plastically before breaking.
Malleability describes how easily a material can be deformed under compression.
Toughness describes a material's ability to absorb energy before fracturing.
Brittleness describes a tendency to fracture with little plastic deformation.
A caliper is a measuring instrument used to measure dimensions.

Digital calipers display measurements electronically.
Outside calipers measure external dimensions.
Inside calipers measure internal dimensions.
A micrometer provides highly precise dimensional measurements.
An outside micrometer measures external dimensions.
A depth micrometer measures depths.
A height gauge measures vertical dimensions from a reference surface.
A ruler can be used for basic dimensional measurements.
A steel rule is commonly used in metalworking.
A square is used to check or mark right angles.
A combination square can perform several layout and measurement tasks.
A surface plate provides a highly flat reference surface.
A scribe is used to mark lines on metal.
Layout dye can make scribed lines easier to see.
Tolerance defines the acceptable variation in a dimension.
A tighter tolerance requires more precise manufacturing.
A loose tolerance allows greater dimensional variation.
Clearance describes the intentional space between mating components.
Interference fit occurs when one component is slightly larger than the opening into which it is inserted.
A press fit uses interference between mating components.
A slip fit allows components to move or slide relative to each other.
Surface finish describes the texture and condition of a machined surface.
A smoother surface finish generally has smaller surface irregularities.
Machining parameters can affect surface finish.
Tool wear can reduce surface quality.
Polishing can improve the appearance and smoothness of a metal surface.
Buffing can produce a highly polished surface.
Rust is a form of corrosion that affects iron and steel.
Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture.
Corrosion is the deterioration of a material through chemical or electrochemical reactions.
Stainless steel has increased resistance to corrosion compared with ordinary carbon steel.
Galvanizing protects steel by applying a layer of zinc.
Paint and coatings can protect metal surfaces from environmental exposure.
Oil can provide temporary corrosion protection for some metal surfaces.
A weld joint can be prepared by cleaning the surfaces before welding.
Removing rust and oil can improve weld quality.
Proper joint preparation can improve penetration and fusion.
A bevel creates an angled edge before certain welding operations.
A root gap is the space between two workpieces at the root of a joint.
Joint design affects weld strength and penetration.
A blueprint is a technical drawing used to communicate manufacturing information.
Engineering drawings specify dimensions, materials, tolerances, and features.
Orthographic projection represents an object using multiple two-dimensional views.
An isometric drawing represents a three-dimensional object in a two-dimensional drawing.
A section view shows internal features by representing part of an object as removed.
A dimension specifies the size or location of a feature.
A technical drawing may contain symbols for surface finish, welding, and tolerances.
A welding symbol communicates information about a weld on an engineering drawing.
A reference line is a major component of a welding symbol.
An arrow connects the welding symbol to the joint location.
Welding symbols can specify weld type, size, length, and other requirements.

A spur gear has straight teeth parallel to its axis.
A helical gear has angled teeth.
A bevel gear transfers motion between intersecting shafts.
A worm gear uses a worm and a worm wheel.
Gear ratios determine the relationship between input and output speed and torque.
A bearing supports rotating or moving components.
Ball bearings use balls between inner and outer races.
Roller bearings use cylindrical or other shaped rollers.
Bearings reduce friction between moving components.
Lubrication helps reduce friction and wear in many bearings.
A shaft is a rotating mechanical component.
A key can prevent a gear or pulley from rotating independently of a shaft.
A keyway is a slot that accepts a key.
A coupling connects two shafts.
A pulley transfers motion using a belt.
A sprocket transfers motion using a chain.
A fastener is a hardware component used to mechanically join parts.
A bolt normally passes through a hole and is secured with a nut.
A screw typically forms or engages threads in a component.
A nut has internal threads that engage with a bolt or threaded shaft.
A washer distributes load under a fastener.
A locknut helps resist loosening.
A rivet permanently joins components through a mechanical fastening process.
Threading creates helical ridges on a surface.
Internal threads are located inside a hole.
External threads are located on the outside of a shaft.
Threads can be used to create adjustable or removable mechanical connections.
Thread pitch describes the distance between corresponding points on adjacent threads.
Threads can be measured using thread gauges.

Bending operations can be performed using presses, brakes, rolls, or specialized tooling.
Springback occurs when metal partially returns toward its original shape after bending.
Bend allowance accounts for material behavior during bending.
The inside radius of a bend affects the resulting shape and stresses.
A hydraulic press uses hydraulic pressure to generate large mechanical forces.
A mechanical press uses mechanical components to generate force.
Presses can be used for bending, forming, punching, and pressing operations.
A press must be operated with appropriate tooling and safety procedures.
A bandsaw uses a continuous toothed blade to cut material.
A horizontal bandsaw is commonly used to cut metal stock.
A vertical bandsaw can be useful for cutting shapes and contours.
Saw blade selection depends on material, thickness, and desired cutting performance.
A plasma cutter uses a high-temperature plasma arc to cut electrically conductive metals.
Plasma cutting can cut steel, stainless steel, and aluminum.
A plasma cutter requires an appropriate power source and compressed gas.
Plasma cutting produces heat, sparks, and molten metal.
An oxy-fuel torch uses fuel gas and oxygen to produce a high-temperature flame.
Oxy-fuel equipment can be used for cutting, heating, and some welding operations.
Oxy-fuel cutting can cut many types of steel.
Torch operation requires proper handling of pressurized gas cylinders and equipment.
Metalworking machines can be manually operated or computer controlled.
Manual machining requires the operator to control machine movements.
CNC machining automates many machine movements using programmed instructions.
Computer-controlled machining can improve repeatability.
Machinists use measurements throughout manufacturing to verify dimensions.
A machinist is a skilled worker who operates machine tools and produces precision components.
A welder joins materials using welding processes.
A fabricator creates structures and components from raw materials.
A blacksmith traditionally shapes heated metal using hammers and anvils.
A toolmaker manufactures specialized tools, dies, molds, and precision components.
A sheet metal worker fabricates and installs components made from sheet metal.
Metalworking requires an understanding of material properties.
The correct tool depends on the material and operation being performed.
Cutting tools must be selected according to the workpiece and machining operation.
Machine setup affects accuracy and safety.
Workpieces should be securely held before machining or cutting.
Loose clothing should be kept away from rotating machinery.
Long hair should be secured around rotating machinery.
Metal chips can be sharp and should not normally be handled with bare hands.
Compressed air should be used carefully because it can propel metal chips and debris.
Business is the activity of producing, selling, or providing goods and services.
A business is an organization that provides goods or services to customers.
A company is an organization created to conduct business activities.
An entrepreneur is a person who creates or manages a business.
Entrepreneurship involves identifying opportunities and creating businesses or products.
A startup is a newly established business designed to develop and sell a product or service.
A small business is a privately owned business with a relatively small number of employees or revenue.
A corporation is a legal business entity that is separate from its owners.
A sole proprietorship is a business owned and operated by one person.
A partnership is a business owned by two or more people.
A limited liability company provides a business structure that can separate owners from certain business liabilities.
A nonprofit organization operates primarily to pursue a mission rather than distribute profits to owners.
A franchise is a business operated using another company's brand and business model under an agreement.
Revenue is the money a business receives from selling goods or services.
Sales revenue is revenue generated from selling products or services.
Profit is the amount remaining after a business subtracts its costs from its revenue.
Gross profit is revenue minus the direct costs associated with producing goods or services.
Net profit is the amount remaining after expenses, taxes, interest, and other costs are accounted for.
A loss occurs when a business's expenses exceed its revenue.
Profit margin measures profit as a percentage of revenue.
A business can increase profit by increasing revenue, reducing costs, or both.
An expense is a cost incurred while operating a business.
Fixed costs generally remain relatively stable as production changes.
Rent is an example of a fixed business cost.
Variable costs change as production or sales volume changes.
Raw materials are often variable costs.
Operating expenses are costs associated with running a business.
Labor costs include wages, salaries, benefits, and other employee-related expenses.
Marketing expenses are costs associated with promoting products or services.
Administrative expenses are costs associated with managing a business.
A budget is a plan for expected income and expenses.
A business budget helps organizations plan how money will be spent.
A forecast is an estimate of future financial or business conditions.
Financial planning involves setting financial goals and determining how to achieve them.
Cash flow describes money moving into and out of a business.

Negative cash flow occurs when more money leaves a business than enters it during a period.
A profitable business can still experience cash-flow problems.
An asset is something valuable that a person or business owns or controls.
Cash is a highly liquid business asset.
Inventory is the stock of goods a business holds for sale.
Equipment is a physical asset used in business operations.
A liability is an obligation or debt owed by a person or business.
A loan is a liability when a business owes money to a lender.
Equity represents an ownership interest in a business.
The basic accounting equation is assets equal liabilities plus equity.
Accounting is the process of recording, organizing, and reporting financial information.
A balance sheet reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.
An income statement reports revenue, expenses, and profit over a period.
A cash flow statement reports changes in cash during a period.
Bookkeeping involves recording financial transactions.
Accounts receivable represents money owed to a business by customers.
Accounts payable represents money a business owes to suppliers or other parties.
An invoice is a document requesting payment for goods or services.
A receipt provides evidence that a payment has been made.
A purchase order is a document used to request goods or services from a supplier.
A transaction is an exchange involving money, goods, services, or other value.
A financial statement summarizes financial information about an organization.
Supply is the quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to sell.
Demand is the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to purchase.
The law of demand generally states that quantity demanded decreases as price increases, other factors being equal.
The law of supply generally states that quantity supplied increases as price increases, other factors being equal.
Supply and demand interact to influence market prices and quantities.
An increase in demand can put upward pressure on prices.
An increase in supply can put downward pressure on prices.
A decrease in supply can put upward pressure on prices.
Equilibrium occurs when quantity supplied equals quantity demanded in a market.
The equilibrium price is the price at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.
A shortage occurs when quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a given price.
A surplus occurs when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a given price.
Market prices can change when supply or demand changes.
A market is a system in which buyers and sellers exchange goods or services.
A consumer is a person or organization that purchases or uses goods and services.
A producer creates goods or provides services.
A supplier provides products, materials, or services to another business.
A distributor helps move products from producers to retailers or customers.
A retailer sells products directly to consumers.
A wholesaler sells goods in larger quantities, often to retailers or businesses.
A product is a good or service offered to customers.
A good is a physical product that can satisfy a consumer need or want.
A service is an activity or benefit provided to a customer.
