Withdrawals decrease the account balance.
Fees decrease the account balance.
Interest payments can increase the account balance.
Interest charges can decrease the account balance.
A cash flow statement tracks cash entering and leaving an organization.
Operating cash flow relates to cash generated or used by normal business operations.
Investing cash flow relates to purchases and sales of investments or long-term assets.
Financing cash flow relates to borrowing, repayment, investment, and distributions involving financing.
Cash flow analysis helps determine whether an organization has enough cash to meet obligations.
A business can receive cash from customers.
A business can spend cash on wages, rent, supplies, taxes, and other expenses.
A business can borrow money to increase available cash.
A business can repay loans using future cash flow.
A business can be profitable while having insufficient cash to pay immediate bills.
Cash flow management is important for maintaining financial stability.
A bank's ledger records financial transactions associated with an account.
A ledger balance represents the balance according to recorded transactions.
Available funds can differ from a ledger balance because of pending transactions or holds.
A cleared transaction has completed the relevant processing stages.
A pending transaction has not yet fully cleared.
A payment processor facilitates the movement of payment information between parties.
A merchant is a business or organization that accepts payments.
A point-of-sale system processes purchases at a business.
Contactless payment allows customers to pay using compatible cards or devices.
A payment terminal reads or receives payment information during a transaction.
A refund returns money to a customer after an eligible purchase has been reversed or returned.
A chargeback is a payment dispute process that can reverse certain card transactions.
A cardholder can dispute certain transactions through the applicable financial institution.
A merchant may issue a refund directly to a customer.
A reversed transaction is a transaction that has been cancelled or undone.
A foreign exchange transaction converts one currency into another.
The exchange rate determines how much of one currency is received for another.
A spread is the difference between certain buying and selling rates.
Currency conversion may involve fees or exchange-rate differences.
International transactions can affect an account balance because of currency conversion.
Banking regulations establish rules governing financial institutions and financial services.
Consumer protection rules can establish rights and responsibilities for banking customers.
Financial institutions may be required to maintain records of certain transactions.
Anti-money-laundering regulations require financial institutions to monitor certain financial activity.
Financial institutions may report certain transactions or suspicious activity to appropriate authorities.
A bank statement can be used to calculate monthly cash flow.
Monthly income can be compared with monthly spending to determine whether cash flow is positive or negative.
Tracking cash inflows and outflows can help identify spending patterns.
A cash-flow deficit occurs when outflows exceed inflows during a period.
A cash-flow surplus occurs when inflows exceed outflows during a period.
A zero balance means that the recorded account balance is exactly zero.
A positive balance means money remains available or owed to the account holder depending on account type.
A negative balance generally means money is owed to the financial institution.
An overdraft can temporarily produce a negative checking account balance.
Bringing an overdrawn account back above zero generally requires depositing or transferring enough money to cover the negative amount and applicable charges.
Banking records can help people understand where their money goes.
Income records show money received.
Expense records show money spent.
Transaction histories provide a chronological record of account activity.
Regularly reviewing account activity can help identify errors, unexpected charges, and unauthorized transactions.
The WannaCry attack was a major ransomware outbreak that began spreading in May 2017.
WannaCry encrypted files on infected computers and demanded payment from victims.
The WannaCry outbreak affected organizations in numerous countries.
WannaCry exploited a Windows vulnerability known as EternalBlue.
EternalBlue exploited a vulnerability in the Server Message Block protocol.
Microsoft released a security update addressing the vulnerability before the WannaCry outbreak.
The WannaCry outbreak demonstrated the importance of installing security updates.
The WannaCry attack affected parts of the United Kingdom's National Health Service.
The WannaCry outbreak disrupted hospitals and medical services in several locations.
A security researcher accidentally activated a mechanism that slowed the original WannaCry outbreak.
WannaCry became one of the most widely known ransomware outbreaks in internet history.
MyDoom was a computer worm that became widespread in 2004.
MyDoom spread primarily through malicious email attachments.
MyDoom became one of the fastest-spreading email worms at the time.
MyDoom generated large amounts of network traffic during its widespread infection.
MyDoom was associated with distributed denial-of-service activity.
MyDoom caused significant disruption to computer systems and internet infrastructure.
MyDoom demonstrated how rapidly email-based malware could spread.
MyDoom variants continued appearing after the original outbreak.
ILOVEYOU was a computer worm that spread through email in 2000.
The ILOVEYOU worm was distributed using an email message with the subject "ILOVEYOU".
The worm used social engineering to encourage recipients to open an attachment.
ILOVEYOU spread rapidly after users opened the malicious attachment.
The outbreak affected millions of computers around the world.
ILOVEYOU caused significant economic damage through disruption and recovery costs.
The incident demonstrated the effectiveness of social engineering in malware distribution.
Melissa was a computer virus that spread through email in 1999.
The Melissa virus used Microsoft Word documents as part of its propagation.
Melissa caused email systems to become heavily overloaded.
The outbreak affected organizations and businesses around the world.
Melissa demonstrated how malicious documents could be used to spread malware.
The Morris Worm was one of the earliest major internet worms.
The Morris Worm was released in 1988.
The worm was created by Robert Tappan Morris.
The Morris Worm spread across parts of the early internet.
The outbreak caused computers to consume excessive system resources.
The Morris Worm became an important event in the history of internet security.
Robert Tappan Morris became the first person convicted under the United States Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.
Code Red was a computer worm discovered in 2001.
Code Red primarily targeted vulnerable Microsoft IIS web servers.
The worm could spread automatically between vulnerable systems.
Code Red infected large numbers of systems in a relatively short period.
The outbreak demonstrated the risks associated with unpatched internet-facing servers.
Code Red was associated with attacks against websites and network infrastructure.
Nimda was a computer worm that spread in 2001.
Nimda used multiple methods to spread between computers.
Nimda could spread through email and compromised websites.
The worm affected both individual computers and network servers.
Nimda became notable for its rapid spread across the internet.
SQL Slammer was a computer worm that spread in 2003.
SQL Slammer exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft SQL Server.
SQL Slammer was extremely small compared with many other malware programs.
The worm spread extremely quickly across vulnerable systems.
SQL Slammer caused significant network congestion.
The outbreak disrupted some internet services and network infrastructure.
SQL Slammer demonstrated how quickly automated worms could spread.
Conficker was a computer worm that began spreading widely in 2008.
Conficker exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft Windows.
Conficker infected millions of computers around the world.
The worm created a large network of compromised computers.
Conficker became one of the most extensively studied malware outbreaks.
Security researchers and technology companies coordinated efforts to contain Conficker.
Stuxnet was a highly sophisticated computer worm discovered in 2010.
Stuxnet targeted industrial control systems.
Stuxnet was designed to interfere with specific industrial equipment.
The malware targeted systems associated with Iran's nuclear program.
Stuxnet demonstrated that malware could affect physical industrial processes.
Stuxnet became an important milestone in the history of cyber warfare.
The sophistication of Stuxnet attracted significant attention from cybersecurity researchers.
NotPetya was a destructive malware outbreak that began in 2017.
NotPetya initially appeared similar to ransomware.
NotPetya caused widespread destruction rather than functioning primarily as ordinary ransomware.
The attack affected organizations around the world.
The incident caused billions of dollars in estimated economic damage.
NotPetya affected shipping companies, manufacturers, hospitals, and other organizations.
The attack demonstrated how malware could spread through interconnected business networks.
The Petya malware family included ransomware that appeared before NotPetya.
Petya could interfere with a computer's ability to boot normally.
Petya became widely known because it targeted disk-related system structures.
NotPetya was later identified as substantially more destructive than traditional ransomware.
The Mirai malware was first discovered in 2016.
Mirai primarily targeted internet-connected devices such as routers and security cameras.
Mirai created a botnet from compromised Internet of Things devices.
The Mirai botnet was used to conduct large distributed denial-of-service attacks.
The Mirai source code was publicly released in 2016.
The release of the source code contributed to the creation of additional IoT botnets.
The 2016 Dyn cyberattack was a major distributed denial-of-service event.
The attack targeted Dyn, a major DNS infrastructure provider.
The attack affected access to several major internet services.
Services affected included websites and platforms that depended on Dyn's infrastructure.
The attack demonstrated the importance of DNS infrastructure to the modern internet.
The incident also demonstrated the potential power of IoT-based botnets.
A distributed denial-of-service attack attempts to overwhelm a service with traffic from many sources.
A DDoS attack can make websites or online services unavailable.
A botnet is a network of compromised computers or devices controlled by an attacker.
IoT botnets can contain large numbers of compromised internet-connected devices.
DDoS attacks can target websites, DNS providers, servers, and network infrastructure.
The 2014 Sony Pictures hack was a major cyberattack against Sony Pictures Entertainment.
Attackers stole and released internal company information.
The incident resulted in the disclosure of employee information and corporate communications.
Several unreleased films were distributed online following the attack.
The attackers also caused disruption to Sony Pictures' computer systems.
The incident received significant international media attention.
The 2013 Target data breach affected millions of customers.
Attackers obtained payment card information from Target systems.
The incident became one of the most prominent retail data breaches of its time.
The breach demonstrated the risks associated with third-party access to corporate networks.
Target later faced significant costs related to the breach.
The Equifax data breach occurred in 2017.
Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an internet-facing application used by Equifax.
The breach exposed sensitive personal information belonging to millions of people.
The exposed information included names, dates of birth, addresses, and other identifying information.
The Equifax incident became one of the most significant data breaches involving a credit reporting company.
The incident highlighted the importance of vulnerability management and security patching.
The Yahoo data breaches affected hundreds of millions of user accounts.
Yahoo disclosed major breaches during the 2010s.
Some Yahoo breaches exposed account information and authentication-related data.
The scale of the breaches made Yahoo's incidents particularly notable.
The breaches contributed to increased public attention on the security of large online platforms.
The Ashley Madison data breach occurred in 2015.
Attackers stole information from the Ashley Madison website.
The attackers later released large amounts of stolen data.
The incident caused significant personal and legal consequences for affected users.
The breach became one of the most widely discussed examples of a privacy-related cyberattack.
The Adobe data breach was disclosed in 2013.
Attackers obtained information associated with millions of Adobe accounts.
The incident involved encrypted passwords and other customer information.
The breach highlighted the importance of secure password storage and account protection.
The Heartbleed vulnerability was publicly disclosed in 2014.
Heartbleed affected certain versions of the OpenSSL cryptographic software library.
Heartbleed could potentially expose sensitive information from vulnerable servers.
The vulnerability received widespread attention because OpenSSL was widely used across the internet.
Heartbleed demonstrated that vulnerabilities in widely used infrastructure software could affect enormous numbers of systems.
Shellshock was a family of vulnerabilities disclosed in 2014.
Shellshock affected the Unix Bash command shell.
The vulnerability could allow attackers to execute commands on vulnerable systems under certain conditions.
Shellshock affected many Unix and Linux-based systems.
The vulnerability received widespread attention because Bash was widely deployed.
The Log4Shell vulnerability was disclosed in 2021.
Log4Shell affected the Apache Log4j Java logging library.
Log4j was widely used in applications and services.
The vulnerability could allow remote code execution under vulnerable configurations.
Log4Shell caused widespread concern because of the enormous number of systems using Log4j.
Organizations around the world worked to identify and patch affected systems.
The SolarWinds cyberattack became widely known in 2020.
Attackers compromised software development and distribution processes associated with SolarWinds.
Malicious code was distributed through compromised software updates.
Organizations that installed affected updates could become compromised.
The incident affected government agencies and private organizations.
The SolarWinds incident demonstrated the risks of software supply-chain attacks.
A supply-chain attack compromises a trusted supplier or software provider to reach downstream targets.
Supply-chain attacks can be difficult to detect because malicious activity can originate from trusted software.
Software dependencies can create security risks when vulnerable components are widely distributed.
Organizations use dependency management and security monitoring to reduce supply-chain risks.
The Colonial Pipeline cyberattack occurred in 2021.
The attack affected Colonial Pipeline, a major fuel pipeline operator in the United States.
The incident caused the company to temporarily shut down parts of its pipeline operations.
The disruption affected fuel distribution in parts of the United States.
The incident demonstrated how cyberattacks could have effects beyond computer systems.
The WannaCry, NotPetya, and Colonial Pipeline incidents demonstrated that cyberattacks can affect physical operations.
Cybersecurity incidents can disrupt hospitals, transportation, manufacturing, energy systems, and other critical infrastructure.
Critical infrastructure includes systems and services essential to the functioning of society.
Cybersecurity is especially important for organizations operating critical infrastructure.
The 2016 United States Democratic National Committee cyberattack involved the theft and publication of political organization emails.
The incident became part of a broader controversy surrounding election-related cybersecurity.
The attack contributed to increased public attention on foreign interference and political cyber operations.
Cybersecurity became a major issue in discussions about election infrastructure.
The 2020 Twitter account takeover affected several high-profile Twitter accounts.
Attackers gained access to accounts belonging to prominent individuals and companies.
The compromised accounts were used to promote a cryptocurrency scam.
The incident demonstrated the risks associated with administrative access to major social media platforms.
The attack also demonstrated how social engineering can be used to compromise internal systems.
The RockYou data breach occurred in 2009.
The breach exposed millions of user passwords.
The exposed passwords became widely used in security research and password analysis.
The incident demonstrated the risks of storing passwords insecurely.
RockYou became particularly notable because the leaked passwords were later used as a common password dataset.
The LinkedIn data breach disclosed in 2012 exposed information associated with millions of accounts.
The breach involved password hashes and other account information.
A large collection of LinkedIn account data was later circulated online.
The incident demonstrated the importance of strong password hashing and unique passwords.
The PlayStation Network outage occurred in 2011.
Sony's PlayStation Network experienced a major security incident and extended service outage.
Personal information associated with millions of accounts was compromised.
The service was unavailable for an extended period.
The incident became one of the most significant gaming-related cybersecurity events of its time.
The 2014 eBay data breach affected a large number of user accounts.
Attackers obtained access to employee credentials and used them to access internal systems.
The incident exposed customer information.
eBay required many users to change their passwords following the breach.
The Capital One data breach occurred in 2019.
The incident exposed personal information associated with millions of customers and applicants.
The breach involved cloud-hosted data.
The incident attracted attention to cloud security and access controls.
Cloud security involves protecting data, applications, and infrastructure hosted in cloud environments.
A data breach occurs when unauthorized individuals gain access to protected information.
A data leak occurs when information becomes available to unauthorized people.
A cyberattack is an intentional attempt to compromise, disrupt, steal, or manipulate computer systems or information.
Malware is software designed to perform malicious or unauthorized actions.
A computer virus is malware that can replicate by attaching itself to other files or programs.
A computer worm can spread between systems without requiring the same type of manual execution as many traditional viruses.
A Trojan is malicious software disguised as legitimate or useful software.
Ransomware is malware that prevents access to data or systems and demands payment.
Spyware is software designed to monitor or collect information without appropriate authorization.
A rootkit is software designed to conceal unauthorized access or malicious activity.
A botnet is a collection of compromised devices controlled by an attacker.
Phishing is a social engineering technique used to trick people into revealing information or performing actions.
Spear phishing is targeted phishing directed at a specific person or organization.
Whaling is a form of phishing that targets high-profile individuals.
Social engineering manipulates people rather than relying entirely on technical vulnerabilities.
Credential theft involves obtaining usernames, passwords, authentication tokens, or similar information.
A password attack attempts to obtain or bypass authentication credentials.
Credential stuffing uses previously compromised username and password combinations against other services.
Password reuse increases the impact of a stolen password.
Multi-factor authentication can reduce the risk associated with stolen passwords.
A security patch is an update designed to fix vulnerabilities or other security problems.
Patch management involves identifying, testing, and deploying software updates.
An unpatched system may remain vulnerable to known security issues.
A zero-day vulnerability is a vulnerability that is unknown or has not yet been fully addressed by the affected vendor.
A zero-day exploit takes advantage of a vulnerability before an effective patch or mitigation is broadly available.
A vulnerability is a weakness that can potentially be exploited to compromise a system.
An exploit is a technique or software that takes advantage of a vulnerability.
A security researcher studies vulnerabilities and security weaknesses.
Responsible disclosure involves reporting security vulnerabilities so they can be addressed appropriately.
Encryption converts information into a form intended to prevent unauthorized parties from reading it.
Decryption converts encrypted information back into a readable form.
End-to-end encryption protects communications so that only intended endpoints can generally access the readable content.
A cryptographic key is information used by a cryptographic algorithm.
Public-key cryptography uses mathematically related public and private keys.
A firewall monitors and controls network traffic according to defined rules.
An intrusion detection system monitors networks or systems for suspicious activity.
An intrusion prevention system can detect and attempt to block certain malicious activity.
Antivirus software detects and removes or quarantines certain types of malware.
Endpoint security protects computers and other network-connected devices.
Security monitoring involves observing systems and networks for suspicious behavior.
A distributed denial-of-service attack uses multiple systems to generate traffic against a target.
A denial-of-service attack attempts to make a service unavailable to legitimate users.
A botnet can be used to generate large amounts of traffic during a DDoS attack.
DDoS attacks can cause temporary outages without necessarily stealing data.
DDoS mitigation involves techniques designed to absorb, filter, or block malicious traffic.
The internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks.
The World Wide Web is a system of websites and resources accessed through the internet.
The Domain Name System translates domain names into network addresses.
DNS is essential for locating internet services using human-readable domain names.
A DNS attack can interfere with the process of locating online services.
A DNS provider can become a critical dependency for many websites.
An internet outage occurs when users lose access to an internet service or network.
A large-scale outage can affect millions of users.
Internet outages can result from technical failures, cyberattacks, configuration errors, or infrastructure problems.
A cascading failure occurs when one failure causes additional systems or services to fail.
Internet infrastructure is highly interconnected, meaning one failure can sometimes affect many dependent services.
A botnet can contain computers, routers, cameras, servers, or other internet-connected devices.
The Internet of Things refers to physical devices that connect to networks and exchange data.
Poorly secured IoT devices can become targets for malware.
Default passwords can create security risks when devices are deployed without proper configuration.
IoT security involves protecting connected physical devices and their associated networks.
The history of internet security includes major malware outbreaks, data breaches, vulnerabilities, and infrastructure attacks.
Major cyber incidents have influenced software security practices and cybersecurity policy.
Large malware outbreaks have encouraged organizations to improve patch management and network security.
Major data breaches have increased public awareness of password security and privacy.
Cybersecurity incidents have demonstrated the importance of backups, authentication, monitoring, and software updates.
The 1990s were a decade marked by major political, technological, economic, and cultural changes.
The 2000s were marked by rapid technological development, major wars, terrorism, economic changes, and globalization.
The Berlin Wall fell in November 1989, contributing to the collapse of communist governments in Eastern Europe.
German reunification occurred in 1990.
The Soviet Union dissolved in December 1991.
The dissolution of the Soviet Union ended the Soviet state and created several independent countries.
The Cold War effectively ended with the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Nelson Mandela was released from prison in 1990.
Nelson Mandela became President of South Africa in 1994.
South Africa held its first fully inclusive national election in 1994.
The end of apartheid became one of the most important political developments of the 1990s.
The Gulf War began in 1990 after Iraq invaded Kuwait.
A United States-led coalition fought Iraqi forces during the Gulf War.
Kuwait was liberated in 1991.
The Gulf War demonstrated the military importance of modern air power and precision weapons.
The Yugoslav Wars began in the early 1990s.
The breakup of Yugoslavia resulted in several armed conflicts.
The Bosnian War occurred from 1992 to 1995.
The Siege of Sarajevo became one of the most infamous events of the Bosnian War.
The Srebrenica massacre occurred in 1995.
The Kosovo War occurred in 1998 and 1999.
The Yugoslav Wars resulted in large numbers of deaths and displaced people.
The Rwandan genocide occurred in 1994.
The genocide resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people.
The Rwandan genocide lasted approximately 100 days.
The genocide became one of the most horrific events of the 1990s.
The international response to the Rwandan genocide became the subject of extensive criticism and debate.
The Oklahoma City bombing occurred in 1995.
The bombing targeted the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City.
The attack killed 168 people.
The Oklahoma City bombing became the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in the United States at the time.
Timothy McVeigh was convicted for his role in the bombing.
The 1993 World Trade Center bombing occurred in New York City.
The bombing targeted the World Trade Center complex.
The attack was intended to cause major structural damage.
The bombing killed six people and injured more than a thousand others.
The event became an important precursor to later terrorist attacks against the World Trade Center.
The Unabomber campaign involved a series of mail bombings in the United States.
The attacks occurred over several decades and continued into the 1990s.
The FBI conducted a long investigation into the Unabomber.
The suspect was identified as Theodore Kaczynski.
Kaczynski was arrested in 1996.
The Columbine High School massacre occurred in 1999.
Two students carried out an attack at Columbine High School in Colorado.
The attack killed 12 students and one teacher.
The Columbine attack became one of the most infamous school shootings in American history.
The incident had a major influence on discussions about school safety and mass violence.
Princess Diana died in a car crash in Paris in 1997.
The death of Princess Diana received enormous international media attention.
Millions of people participated in mourning events following her death.
The event became one of the most widely covered celebrity deaths of the twentieth century.
The death of Diana, Princess of Wales, caused extensive public mourning in the United Kingdom and around the world.
The funeral of Princess Diana was watched by hundreds of millions of people worldwide.
The Heaven's Gate mass suicide occurred in 1997.
Members of the Heaven's Gate group died in California.
The event became one of the most infamous incidents involving a religious cult in modern American history.
The Branch Davidians were involved in a deadly standoff with federal authorities in Waco, Texas.
The Waco siege began in 1993.
The siege ended in a fire that killed many people inside the compound.
The Waco incident became highly controversial and influenced later extremist movements.
The 1992 Los Angeles riots occurred following the acquittal of four police officers involved in the beating of Rodney King.
The riots lasted several days.
The unrest resulted in deaths, injuries, arrests, and extensive property damage.
The Los Angeles riots became a major event in discussions about policing and racial tensions in the United States.
The Rodney King video became an important example of the influence of consumer-recorded video on public opinion.
The footage showed police officers beating Rodney King.
The recording was widely broadcast by television networks.
The Tiananmen Square protests occurred in China in 1989.
The Chinese government used military force to suppress the protests.
The Tiananmen Square crackdown became one of the most controversial political events associated with the end of the 1980s and the beginning of the 1990s.
The image of a lone protester standing in front of tanks became internationally famous.
The Good Friday Agreement was signed in 1998.
The agreement helped establish a political framework for peace in Northern Ireland.
The agreement significantly reduced large-scale political violence associated with the Troubles.
The Troubles were a period of conflict in Northern Ireland lasting from the late 1960s until the 1990s.
The conflict involved republican and loyalist paramilitary organizations as well as British security forces.
The Good Friday Agreement became a major milestone in ending the conflict.
Hong Kong was transferred from British to Chinese sovereignty in 1997.
The handover ended more than 150 years of British colonial rule in Hong Kong.
Hong Kong became a Special Administrative Region of China.
The Channel Tunnel opened in 1994.
The Channel Tunnel connects the United Kingdom and France beneath the English Channel.
The tunnel became one of the most significant transportation engineering projects of the twentieth century.
The European Union was formally established in 1993.
The Maastricht Treaty created the European Union.
The European Union developed from earlier European economic and political organizations.
The euro was introduced as an electronic currency in 1999.
Euro banknotes and coins entered circulation in 2002.
The North American Free Trade Agreement came into effect in 1994.
NAFTA created a major free-trade area between Canada, the United States, and Mexico.
The agreement significantly affected trade and economic relationships in North America.
The World Wide Web became increasingly popular during the 1990s.
The first web browser was developed before the 1990s, but widespread public adoption accelerated during the decade.
The commercialization of the internet transformed communication, business, and entertainment.
The dot-com boom caused internet companies to receive enormous amounts of investment.
The dot-com bubble reached its peak around 2000.
The dot-com bubble burst in the early 2000s.
Many internet companies failed after the dot-com bubble burst.
Amazon was founded in 1994.
Amazon originally began as an online bookstore.
The company later expanded into many categories of online commerce and technology.
The growth of Amazon became an important part of the rise of e-commerce.
Google was founded in 1998.
Google began as a search engine project created by Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
Google became one of the most influential internet companies in the world.
Search engines became increasingly important as the World Wide Web expanded.
Microsoft released Windows 95 in 1995.
Windows 95 became one of the most commercially successful personal computer operating systems.
Windows 95 helped popularize graphical computing and internet connectivity among home users.
The launch of Windows 95 became a major event in consumer technology.
The Y2K problem was a computer programming issue associated with dates near the year 2000.
Many older computer systems represented years using two digits.
There were concerns that systems could misinterpret the year 2000.
Governments and businesses spent significant resources preparing for Y2K.
The transition into 2000 caused fewer major disruptions than many predictions had suggested.
The first version of the PlayStation was released internationally during the 1990s.
The PlayStation became one of the most successful video game consoles of the decade.
Nintendo released the Nintendo 64 in 1996.
Sega released the Dreamcast in 1998.
The 1990s were an important decade for the transition to three-dimensional video games.
The Pokémon franchise became a global cultural phenomenon during the late 1990s.
Pokémon games were originally released for Nintendo's Game Boy.
The Pokémon animated television series became internationally popular.
Pokémon merchandise became a major commercial success.
The Tamagotchi became a popular electronic toy during the 1990s.
Tamagotchi simulated a virtual pet that required regular attention.
The device became an international fad.
The Spice Girls became one of the most commercially successful pop groups of the 1990s.
The group popularized the phrase "girl power."
The Spice Girls became a major part of 1990s pop culture.
The Backstreet Boys became one of the most commercially successful boy bands of the late 1990s and early 2000s.
Their popularity contributed to the global boy-band phenomenon.
The Titanic sank in April 1912.
The RMS Titanic disaster remained one of the most famous maritime disasters throughout the 1990s and 2000s.
James Cameron's film Titanic was released in 1997.
Titanic became one of the highest-grossing films in history at the time.
The film won numerous Academy Awards.
The film Jurassic Park was released in 1993.
Jurassic Park became a major commercial and cultural success.
The film helped popularize computer-generated visual effects.
The Matrix was released in 1999.
The Matrix became famous for its science-fiction themes and visual effects.
The 1998 World Cup was held in France.
France won the 1998 FIFA World Cup.
The 1994 FIFA World Cup was held in the United States.
Brazil won the 1994 FIFA World Cup.
The 1996 Summer Olympics were held in Atlanta.
The 1996 Olympics were affected by a bombing at Centennial Olympic Park.
The bombing killed two people and injured more than one hundred others.
Eric Rudolph was later convicted for the bombing.
The 1998 ice storm affected parts of eastern Canada and the northeastern United States.
The storm caused widespread power outages and infrastructure damage.
Quebec, Ontario, and parts of the northeastern United States were heavily affected.
The disaster became one of Canada's most significant natural disasters of the 1990s.
Hurricane Andrew struck the United States in 1992.
Hurricane Andrew caused severe destruction in Florida and Louisiana.
The hurricane became one of the most destructive hurricanes in United States history at the time.
The 1997 Asian financial crisis affected several economies in East and Southeast Asia.
Currency values and financial markets declined sharply in several countries.
The crisis caused recessions and financial instability in affected economies.
The International Monetary Fund became heavily involved in responding to the crisis.
The Enron scandal became one of the most infamous corporate scandals of the early 2000s.
Enron was an American energy company that collapsed in 2001.
The company used complex accounting practices to conceal financial problems.
The scandal resulted in criminal convictions and major financial losses.
The Enron scandal contributed to the passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.
WorldCom collapsed in 2002 after a major accounting scandal.
WorldCom had improperly accounted for billions of dollars in expenses.
The scandal became one of the largest accounting fraud cases in United States history at the time.
The WorldCom collapse contributed to increased scrutiny of corporate accounting.
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act was passed in the United States in 2002.
The law increased requirements for corporate financial reporting and internal controls.
The legislation was partly a response to major corporate scandals such as Enron and WorldCom.
The September 11 attacks occurred in the United States on September 11, 2001.
Nineteen terrorists associated with al-Qaeda hijacked four commercial airplanes.
Two aircraft were flown into the World Trade Center towers in New York City.
Another aircraft was flown into the Pentagon.
United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers and crew attempted to regain control.
Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the attacks.
The September 11 attacks became one of the defining events of the early twenty-first century.
The attacks led to major changes in United States foreign policy and national security.
The attacks led to the United States invasion of Afghanistan.
The attacks also contributed to the creation of the United States Department of Homeland Security.
The War in Afghanistan began in 2001 following the September 11 attacks.
The United States and allied forces invaded Afghanistan in October 2001.
The Taliban government was removed from power during the initial invasion.
The conflict continued for many years.
The Afghanistan War became one of the longest military conflicts in United States history.
The Iraq War began in 2003.
A United States-led coalition invaded Iraq in March 2003.
The government of Saddam Hussein was overthrown.
Saddam Hussein was captured in December 2003.
The Iraq War became highly controversial internationally.
The conflict resulted in extensive casualties, displacement, and political instability.
Saddam Hussein was the president of Iraq from 1979 until 2003.
Saddam Hussein was captured by United States forces in 2003.
Saddam Hussein was later tried and convicted by an Iraqi court.
Saddam Hussein was executed in 2006.
The Abu Ghraib prisoner abuse scandal became public in 2004.
Photographs showed American military personnel abusing prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq.
The photographs caused international outrage.
The scandal became a major controversy surrounding the Iraq War.
The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami occurred on December 26, 2004.
The earthquake occurred off the coast of Sumatra.
The resulting tsunami affected countries around the Indian Ocean.
Hundreds of thousands of people were killed.
The disaster became one of the deadliest natural disasters in modern history.
Hurricane Katrina struck the United States in 2005.
The hurricane caused catastrophic flooding in New Orleans.
The failure of parts of the city's flood protection system contributed to the disaster.
Hurricane Katrina caused extensive destruction along the Gulf Coast.
More than a thousand people died as a result of the disaster.
The response to Hurricane Katrina became the subject of significant political controversy.
The 2008 financial crisis became one of the most severe global economic crises since the Great Depression.
The crisis was strongly associated with problems in the United States housing and financial sectors.
The collapse of Lehman Brothers occurred in September 2008.
The failure of Lehman Brothers intensified global financial instability.
Governments and central banks implemented emergency measures to stabilize financial systems.
The crisis caused recessions, unemployment, and major financial losses in many countries.
The United States government provided emergency financial assistance to major financial institutions during the 2008 crisis.
The Troubled Asset Relief Program was created in 2008.
TARP was intended to stabilize the United States financial system.
The financial crisis led to extensive debate about financial regulation.
The subprime mortgage crisis was an important component of the 2008 financial crisis.
Subprime mortgages were loans made to borrowers with weaker credit profiles.
Large numbers of mortgage defaults contributed to losses in financial markets.
Mortgage-backed securities became heavily affected by the collapse of housing-related assets.
The housing bubble in the United States expanded during the early 2000s.
Housing prices increased significantly in many regions.
The housing market later declined sharply.
The housing crash contributed to financial losses and the broader economic crisis.
The iPhone was introduced by Apple in 2007.
The iPhone combined mobile telephone functions with internet connectivity and a touchscreen interface.
The iPhone helped accelerate the smartphone industry.
Smartphones became increasingly important during the late 2000s.
Facebook was founded in 2004.
Facebook initially focused on connecting university students.
The platform later expanded to users around the world.
Facebook became one of the largest social networking platforms of the 2000s.
YouTube was launched in 2005.
YouTube allowed users to upload and share video online.
The platform rapidly became one of the most popular video websites.
YouTube changed how people distributed and consumed online video.
Wikipedia was launched in 2001.
Wikipedia became one of the world's largest collaborative encyclopedias.
The site allowed volunteers to create and edit encyclopedia articles.
Wikipedia became an important source of general information on the internet.
Napster became famous for enabling users to share music files over the internet.
Napster launched in 1999.
The service became one of the most influential examples of peer-to-peer file sharing.
The music industry sued Napster over copyright issues.
Napster was eventually shut down in its original form.
The Napster controversy influenced the development of digital music distribution.
The MP3 format became widely popular during the 1990s and 2000s.
MP3 compression made digital music files substantially smaller than uncompressed audio.
Portable digital music players became increasingly popular.
The growth of digital music changed the music industry's business model.
The Nintendo Wii was released in 2006.
The Wii used motion-sensitive controllers as a major part of its gameplay.
The console attracted many people who had not traditionally been regular video game players.
The Xbox 360 was released in 2005.
The PlayStation 3 was released in 2006.
The Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 became major competitors in the seventh generation of video game consoles.
The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990.
Hubble provided detailed astronomical observations from orbit above Earth's atmosphere.
The telescope produced many famous images of galaxies, nebulae, and other astronomical objects.
Hubble became one of the most famous scientific instruments in history.
The Mars Pathfinder mission landed on Mars in 1997.
The mission deployed the Sojourner rover.
Sojourner became one of the first successful robotic rovers to operate on the surface of Mars.
The mission helped demonstrate technologies for future Mars exploration.
The International Space Station began receiving its first major components in 1998.
The International Space Station became an international scientific and engineering project.
Astronauts from multiple countries have lived and worked aboard the station.
Dolly the sheep was born in 1996.
Dolly became the first mammal widely recognized as successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell.
The announcement of Dolly's cloning caused major scientific and ethical debates.
The event increased public interest in cloning and biotechnology.
The Human Genome Project was officially completed in 2003.
The project produced a reference sequence of much of the human genome.
The Human Genome Project became one of the largest collaborative scientific projects in history.
The project accelerated research in genetics and medicine.
The first known exoplanets orbiting a Sun-like star were discovered in the 1990s.
The discovery of exoplanets demonstrated that planets exist outside our solar system.
Exoplanet research expanded rapidly during the 2000s.
The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997.
The agreement established international commitments related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The Kyoto Protocol became an important milestone in international climate policy.
The SARS outbreak occurred in 2002 and 2003.
Severe acute respiratory syndrome spread to multiple countries.
The outbreak was caused by a previously unknown coronavirus.
International health organizations coordinated efforts to contain the outbreak.
The SARS outbreak demonstrated the potential for infectious diseases to spread rapidly through international travel.
The H5N1 avian influenza outbreak caused international concern during the 2000s.
H5N1 primarily affected birds but also infected some humans.
Governments increased disease surveillance and pandemic preparedness.
The 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic began in 2009.
The pandemic was caused by a novel strain of influenza A virus.
The virus spread rapidly between countries.
The World Health Organization declared an influenza pandemic in 2009.
The 1990s saw the rapid growth of personal computers and home internet access.
The 2000s saw broadband internet become increasingly common.
Wireless networking became increasingly popular during the 2000s.
Online shopping became increasingly mainstream during the 2000s.
Social networking became a major part of internet culture during the 2000s.
The 1990s and 2000s saw the transition from analog media toward digital media.
CDs became a dominant music format during the 1990s.
DVDs became a major home-video format during the late 1990s and 2000s.
Digital downloads increasingly replaced physical media for some forms of entertainment.
Streaming services began emerging toward the end of the 2000s.
The 1990s and 2000s were marked by rapid globalization.
International trade expanded significantly during the period.
The internet made communication between countries faster and easier.
Global supply chains became increasingly important to businesses.
International terrorism became a major geopolitical concern during the 2000s.
The 1990s and 2000s included major changes in the political structure of Europe.
Several former communist countries transitioned toward democratic political systems and market economies.
The expansion of the European Union increased economic and political integration across Europe.
The 1990s and 2000s saw major changes in the way people communicated.
Email became a common method of communication.
Instant messaging became popular among internet users.
Mobile phones became increasingly common.
Text messaging became an important form of everyday communication.
Social media began transforming online communication during the second half of the 2000s.
Brazil won the 1970 FIFA World Cup.
Brazil defeated Italy 4-1 in the 1970 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1970 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Mexico.
Pelé played for Brazil during the 1970 FIFA World Cup.
Brazil became the first country to win the FIFA World Cup three times in 1970.
Gerd Müller was the top scorer of the 1970 FIFA World Cup with 10 goals.
West Germany won the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
West Germany defeated the Netherlands 2-1 in the 1974 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1974 FIFA World Cup was hosted by West Germany.
Johan Cruyff played for the Netherlands during the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
The Netherlands reached the final despite losing to West Germany.
Grzegorz Lato won the Golden Boot at the 1974 FIFA World Cup with 7 goals.
Argentina won the 1978 FIFA World Cup.
Argentina defeated the Netherlands 3-1 after extra time in the 1978 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1978 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Argentina.
Mario Kempes scored twice in the 1978 FIFA World Cup final.
Mario Kempes was the top scorer of the 1978 FIFA World Cup with 6 goals.
Italy won the 1982 FIFA World Cup.
Italy defeated West Germany 3-1 in the 1982 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1982 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Spain.
Paolo Rossi scored 6 goals during the 1982 FIFA World Cup.
Paolo Rossi won the Golden Boot at the 1982 FIFA World Cup.
Italy goalkeeper Dino Zoff became the oldest captain to lift the FIFA World Cup at the time.
Argentina won the 1986 FIFA World Cup.
Argentina defeated West Germany 3-2 in the 1986 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1986 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Mexico.
Diego Maradona captained Argentina during the 1986 FIFA World Cup.
Diego Maradona scored the famous "Hand of God" goal against England.
Diego Maradona also scored the famous "Goal of the Century" against England.
Argentina won the 1986 FIFA World Cup with Diego Maradona as its most famous player.
West Germany won the 1990 FIFA World Cup.
West Germany defeated Argentina 1-0 in the 1990 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1990 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Italy.
Lothar Matthäus captained West Germany during the 1990 FIFA World Cup.
Salvatore Schillaci won the Golden Boot at the 1990 FIFA World Cup.
West Germany became the first team to win the FIFA World Cup three times under the same national identity before reunified Germany later won again.
Brazil won the 1994 FIFA World Cup.
Brazil defeated Italy 3-2 on penalties after a 0-0 draw in the 1994 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1994 FIFA World Cup was hosted by the United States.
Romário was one of Brazil's most important players during the 1994 FIFA World Cup.
Roberto Baggio missed Italy's final penalty in the 1994 FIFA World Cup shootout.
Brazil became the first country to win four FIFA World Cups.
France won the 1998 FIFA World Cup.
France defeated Brazil 3-0 in the 1998 FIFA World Cup final.
The 1998 FIFA World Cup was hosted by France.
Zinedine Zidane scored twice in the 1998 FIFA World Cup final.
France won its first FIFA World Cup in 1998.
Davor Šuker won the Golden Boot at the 1998 FIFA World Cup with 6 goals.
Brazil won the 2002 FIFA World Cup.
Brazil defeated Germany 2-0 in the 2002 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2002 FIFA World Cup was hosted jointly by South Korea and Japan.
Ronaldo scored both goals in the 2002 FIFA World Cup final.
Ronaldo scored 8 goals during the 2002 FIFA World Cup.
Brazil won its fifth FIFA World Cup in 2002.
Brazil remains the only country to have won five FIFA World Cups.
Italy won the 2006 FIFA World Cup.
Italy defeated France 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the 2006 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2006 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Germany.
Zinedine Zidane was sent off in the final after headbutting Marco Materazzi.
Fabio Grosso scored Italy's winning penalty in the 2006 FIFA World Cup shootout.
Miroslav Klose won the Golden Boot at the 2006 FIFA World Cup with 5 goals.
Spain won the 2010 FIFA World Cup.
Spain defeated the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in the 2010 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2010 FIFA World Cup was hosted by South Africa.
Andrés Iniesta scored the winning goal in the 2010 FIFA World Cup final.
Spain won its first FIFA World Cup in 2010.
Spain became the first European team to win a FIFA World Cup held outside Europe or the Americas.
Thomas Müller won the Golden Boot at the 2010 FIFA World Cup with 5 goals.
Germany won the 2014 FIFA World Cup.
Germany defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2014 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2014 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Brazil.
Mario Götze scored the winning goal in the 2014 FIFA World Cup final.
Germany became the first European team to win the FIFA World Cup in South America.
James Rodríguez won the Golden Boot at the 2014 FIFA World Cup with 6 goals.
France won the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
France defeated Croatia 4-2 in the 2018 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2018 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Russia.
Kylian Mbappé scored in the 2018 FIFA World Cup final.
Kylian Mbappé became one of the youngest players to score in a FIFA World Cup final.
Harry Kane won the Golden Boot at the 2018 FIFA World Cup with 6 goals.
France won its second FIFA World Cup in 2018.
Argentina won the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
Argentina defeated France 4-2 on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the 2022 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar.
Lionel Messi captained Argentina during the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
Lionel Messi scored twice in the 2022 FIFA World Cup final.
Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick in the 2022 FIFA World Cup final.
Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 8 goals.
Lionel Messi won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.
Argentina won its third FIFA World Cup in 2022.
Argentina's 2022 victory gave Lionel Messi his first FIFA World Cup title.
Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup final was played on July 19, 2026.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup final was played at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Ferran Torres scored Spain's winning goal in the 106th minute of the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
Argentina finished as runner-up in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
England finished third at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Spain won its second men's FIFA World Cup in 2026.
Spain previously won the FIFA World Cup in 2010.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup was the first World Cup to feature 48 teams.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Canada, Mexico, and the United States.
Spain's 2026 victory made it the reigning men's and women's FIFA World Cup champion at the same time, a first in World Cup history.
