sentences.text: Woodworking is the craft of shaping, joining, and finishing wood to create useful or decorative objects.
Woodworking can be practiced as a hobby, trade, or professional craft.
Woodworkers can create furniture, cabinets, boxes, instruments, bowls, toys, and decorative objects.
Woodworking includes techniques such as sawing, planing, carving, sanding, drilling, turning, and joinery.
Wood is commonly classified as hardwood or softwood.
Hardwoods generally come from deciduous trees.
Softwoods generally come from coniferous trees.
Oak is a common hardwood used for furniture and cabinetry.
Maple is a hard wood commonly used for furniture, flooring, and cutting boards.
Walnut is valued for its dark colour and attractive grain.
Cherry is commonly used for furniture and cabinetry.
Pine is an inexpensive softwood commonly used for construction and woodworking projects.
Cedar is known for its resistance to decay and characteristic aroma.
Spruce is a softwood commonly used in construction and some musical instruments.
Fir is a common construction softwood.
Ash is a strong hardwood commonly used for furniture and tool handles.
Grain describes the direction and pattern of wood fibres.
End grain is the exposed surface at the end of a board.
Face grain refers to the broad surface of a board.
Edge grain refers to the narrower longitudinal surface of a board.
Wood grain direction affects how wood should be cut, planed, and sanded.
Working against the grain can produce tear-out.
Tear-out occurs when pieces of wood are torn away rather than cleanly cut.
Lumber is wood that has been processed into boards or other usable dimensions.
Rough lumber has not been fully surfaced or dimensioned.
S4S means lumber that has been surfaced on all four sides.
Kiln-dried lumber has been dried in a controlled kiln.
Air-dried lumber is dried naturally under controlled conditions.
Wood moisture content affects the stability of lumber.
Wood can expand and contract as its moisture content changes.
Plywood is an engineered wood product made from layers of veneer.
The grain direction of adjacent plywood layers is generally arranged differently for strength and stability.
Medium-density fiberboard is commonly called MDF.
MDF is made from wood fibres combined with resin and compressed into panels.
Particleboard is made from wood particles bonded together.
Oriented strand board is an engineered panel made from oriented wood strands.
Veneer is a thin layer of wood applied to another material.
Solid wood is made from natural wood rather than reconstructed wood fibres or particles.
A measuring tape is used to measure lengths.
A ruler is used for relatively short measurements.
A combination square can be used for measuring and marking angles.
A try square is used to check whether surfaces or edges are square.
A marking gauge can scribe a line parallel to an edge.
A marking knife can create precise layout lines.
A pencil can be used for general woodworking marks.
A bevel gauge can transfer or measure angles.
A handsaw is a manually operated saw used to cut wood.
A backsaw has a reinforced back that helps stabilize its blade.
A coping saw has a thin blade used for curved cuts.
A Japanese pull saw cuts primarily when the blade is pulled toward the user.
A tenon saw is commonly used for accurate joinery cuts.
A dovetail saw is a small backsaw designed for fine joinery.
A circular saw uses a rotating circular blade.
A table saw uses a circular blade mounted beneath a table surface.
A miter saw is designed primarily for crosscuts and angled cuts.
A band saw uses a continuous loop of blade.
A jigsaw uses a reciprocating blade and is useful for curved cuts.
A rip cut follows the grain direction of wood.
A crosscut cuts across the grain direction.
A miter cut is an angled cut, commonly made at 45 degrees.
A bevel cut changes the angle across the thickness of a board.
A compound cut combines a miter angle and a bevel angle.
A kerf is the width of material removed by a saw blade.
A hand plane removes thin layers of wood from a surface.
A smoothing plane is used to create a fine surface.
A jack plane is a versatile plane used for general stock preparation.
A jointer plane can be used for flattening and straightening long edges.
A block plane is a compact plane commonly used for trimming and end grain.
A rabbet plane is designed to cut rabbets.
A spokeshave is used to shape curved wooden surfaces.
A chisel is a cutting tool used to remove or shape wood.
A bench chisel is a general-purpose woodworking chisel.
A mortise chisel is designed for cutting mortises.
A carving chisel is used for detailed wood carving.
A mallet can be used to strike a chisel during woodworking.
A wooden mallet is commonly used with chisels because it can reduce damage to the chisel handle.
A rasp removes wood using a coarse toothed surface.
A file can refine or shape certain wooden surfaces.
A scraper removes thin layers of material from wood.
A card scraper is a thin piece of hardened steel used for fine surface preparation.
A drawknife can remove material from wood and is commonly associated with rough shaping.
A drill creates holes in wood.
A drill bit is a cutting tool used to create holes.
A brad-point drill bit is designed specifically for drilling clean holes in wood.
A Forstner bit can create flat-bottomed holes.
A spade bit can create relatively large holes quickly.
A hole saw cuts larger circular holes.
A countersink creates a recess that allows a screw head to sit flush or below the surface.
A drill press provides controlled drilling using a fixed machine.
A screwdriver is used to drive or remove screws.
A screw is a mechanical fastener with threads that grip material.
A nail is a fastener driven into wood.
A brad nail is a thin nail commonly used for small woodworking projects and trim.
Wood glue is commonly used to bond wooden components.
Clamps hold pieces together while glue cures or while work is being performed.
A bench vise holds a workpiece securely.
A woodworking vise is designed specifically for holding wooden workpieces.
A bar clamp can apply pressure across relatively large assemblies.
A pipe clamp can be used to clamp wide assemblies.
A spring clamp provides relatively light clamping pressure.
A quick-release clamp allows rapid adjustment and removal.
Joinery is the process of connecting pieces of wood.
A butt joint joins the end or edge of one piece directly against another.
A miter joint joins pieces at an angle.
A lap joint overlaps two pieces of wood.
A half-lap joint removes material from both pieces so they overlap flush.
A rabbet is a rectangular recess cut along an edge or end of a board.
A dado is a groove cut across the grain that receives another piece of wood.
A groove is a channel cut into a board.
A tongue is a projecting section designed to fit into a groove.
A tongue-and-groove joint connects matching projecting and recessed profiles.
A mortise is a cavity cut into a piece of wood.
A tenon is a projecting section designed to fit into a mortise.
A mortise-and-tenon joint connects a tenon with a matching mortise.
A dovetail joint uses interlocking angled pins and tails.
Dovetail joints are commonly used in drawers and fine cabinetry.
A box joint uses interlocking rectangular fingers.
A dowel joint uses cylindrical wooden pins to align and connect pieces.
A biscuit joint uses thin compressed-wood biscuits inserted into matching slots.
A pocket-hole joint uses an angled hole and screw to join pieces of wood.
Edge joining connects boards along their edges to create a wider panel.
A glue-up is an assembly of multiple pieces bonded together.
A panel can be created by edge-gluing several boards together.
Wood movement must be considered when designing large wooden panels.
Wooden furniture can fail when joints do not accommodate normal wood movement.
Sanding removes small amounts of material to smooth a wooden surface.
Sandpaper is available in different grit sizes.
Lower grit numbers generally represent coarser abrasive particles.
Higher grit numbers generally represent finer abrasive particles.
Sanding usually progresses from coarser abrasives toward finer abrasives.
An orbital sander uses a rapidly moving sanding pad.
A random orbital sander combines orbital motion with rotation.
A sanding block provides a flat surface for hand sanding.
Sanding with the grain can reduce visible scratches.
Wood finishing protects or changes the appearance of a wooden surface.
A finish can enhance the colour and appearance of wood.
Oil finishes penetrate into the wood to varying degrees.
Varnish forms a protective film over the wood.
Polyurethane is a commonly used protective wood finish.
Shellac is a traditional wood finish.
Lacquer is a fast-drying finish used on many wooden objects.
Wax can provide a smooth feel and additional surface protection.
Wood stain changes the colour of wood without necessarily forming the same type of protective film as a finish.
Paint covers the natural appearance of wood with an opaque layer.
Wood filler is used to fill holes, gaps, or imperfections in wood.
Wood putty can be used to repair certain surface imperfections.
A knot is a naturally occurring area where a branch grew from the tree.
Wood can contain cracks, checks, knots, and other natural defects.
Checks are cracks that develop along the grain.
Warping occurs when a board changes shape.
Cupping causes a board to curve across its width.
Bowing causes a board to curve along its length.
Twisting causes different corners of a board to move out of plane.
A straightedge is used to check whether an edge or surface is straight.
A winding stick can help identify twist in a board.
Flattening removes high areas from a wooden surface.
Jointing creates a flat face or straight edge.
Thickness planing makes a board more uniform in thickness.
A planer is a machine used to reduce the thickness of lumber and create a more uniform surface.
A jointer is used to flatten a face or straighten an edge.
A jointer and planer perform different but complementary stock-preparation tasks.
Woodturning is the process of shaping wood while it rotates on a lathe.
A wood lathe rotates a workpiece around an axis.
A bowl gouge is commonly used for turning bowls.
A spindle gouge is commonly used for turning cylindrical or spindle-shaped work.
A parting tool can separate or cut grooves into a rotating workpiece.
A skew chisel can create fine cuts on a wood lathe.
A faceplate can hold certain bowl-shaped or irregular workpieces on a lathe.
Wood carving is the process of shaping wood with cutting tools.
Relief carving creates a raised or recessed design on a surface.
Whittling is a form of carving commonly performed with a knife.
A carving gouge has a curved cutting edge.
A V-tool creates V-shaped grooves in carved designs.
Wood sculpture can involve carving, shaping, sanding, and finishing.
Cabinetmaking focuses on constructing cabinets and other casework.
Casework refers to box-like wooden structures such as cabinets and bookcases.
A cabinet carcass is the main structural body of a cabinet.
A face frame can reinforce and visually finish the front of a cabinet.
A drawer is a sliding storage compartment.
Drawer runners or slides allow a drawer to move in and out.
Dovetail joints are traditionally associated with high-quality drawer construction.
A cabinet door can be attached using hinges.
A hinge allows a door or lid to pivot.
Furniture woodworking includes the construction of tables, chairs, desks, cabinets, and other furnishings.
A tabletop is the horizontal upper surface of a table.
An apron is a structural frame component beneath a tabletop.
A furniture leg supports the main body of a piece of furniture.
A stretcher can connect furniture legs and improve structural stability.
A chair requires joints capable of handling repeated loads and movement.
A workbench provides a stable surface for woodworking.
A woodworking shop may contain benches, saws, planers, jointers, routers, drills, and sanding equipment.
Dust collection systems remove sawdust and wood particles from woodworking machinery.
Wood dust can be hazardous when inhaled.
Respiratory protection may be required depending on the environment and applicable safety procedures.
Eye protection helps protect against flying particles.
Hearing protection can reduce exposure to loud woodworking machinery.
Woodworking machines can cause serious injuries if used improperly.
Woodworkers should receive appropriate training before operating unfamiliar machinery.
Machine guards should be used as intended.
Loose clothing and jewelry can become caught in moving machinery.
Hands should be kept away from cutting tools and blades.
Woodworkers should not attempt to clear a jammed machine while it is running.
Machines should be turned off before maintenance or adjustment.
A machine should be allowed to stop completely before certain cleaning or adjustment tasks.
Kickback occurs when a workpiece is unexpectedly thrown back toward the operator.
Kickback is a significant hazard associated with certain woodworking machines.
Push sticks and push blocks can help keep hands away from cutting areas.
The correct safety procedures depend on the specific woodworking machine and operation.
Mathematics is the study of numbers, quantities, structures, patterns, relationships, and change.
Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics concerned with numbers and basic operations.
Algebra studies symbols and relationships between quantities.
Geometry studies shapes, sizes, positions, and spatial relationships.
Trigonometry studies relationships between angles and sides of triangles.
Calculus studies change, rates of change, and accumulation.
Statistics studies the collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data.
Probability studies the likelihood of events occurring.
Number theory studies the properties of integers and whole numbers.
Discrete mathematics studies mathematical structures that are fundamentally countable or separate.
Linear algebra studies vectors, matrices, and linear transformations.
Set theory studies collections of mathematical objects.
Logic studies valid reasoning and relationships between statements.
The four basic arithmetic operations are addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Addition combines quantities.
Subtraction determines the difference between quantities.
Multiplication represents repeated addition or scaling.
Division distributes a quantity into equal parts or determines how many times one quantity contains another.
A number divided by zero is undefined.
Zero is the additive identity because adding zero does not change a number.
One is the multiplicative identity because multiplying a number by one does not change it.
A positive number is greater than zero.
A negative number is less than zero.
An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero.
Natural numbers are commonly used for counting, although definitions vary regarding whether zero is included.
A rational number can be expressed as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
An irrational number cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.
Real numbers include both rational and irrational numbers.
Complex numbers contain a real component and an imaginary component.
The absolute value of a number represents its distance from zero on the number line.
The absolute value of a positive number is the number itself.
The absolute value of a negative number is its positive counterpart.
The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself.
The cube of a number is the number multiplied by itself three times.
The square root of a nonnegative number is a number that produces the original number when squared.
The cube root of a number is a number that produces the original number when cubed.
A prime number is a positive integer greater than one with exactly two positive divisors.
The number 2 is the only even prime number.
The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
A composite number has more than two positive divisors.
Every integer greater than one can be expressed as a product of prime numbers.
Prime factorization represents a number as a product of prime factors.
A factor divides another number without leaving a remainder.
A multiple is the result of multiplying a number by an integer.
The greatest common factor is the largest positive factor shared by two or more numbers.
The least common multiple is the smallest positive multiple shared by two or more positive integers.
Divisibility rules can determine whether a number is divisible by certain integers without performing full division.
A fraction represents a quantity as a ratio of two numbers.
The number above the fraction bar is the numerator.
The number below the fraction bar is the denominator.
A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator.
An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator.
A mixed number contains a whole-number part and a fractional part.
Equivalent fractions represent the same value.
Fractions can be added by finding a common denominator.
Fractions can be multiplied by multiplying their numerators and denominators.
Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal.
A decimal represents a number using powers of ten.
A terminating decimal has a finite number of decimal places.
A repeating decimal contains a digit or sequence of digits that repeats indefinitely.
Every rational number has a decimal representation that either terminates or repeats.
Irrational numbers have nonterminating, nonrepeating decimal representations.
A percentage represents a quantity as a fraction of one hundred.
The symbol percent means per hundred.
A percentage can be converted to a decimal by dividing by one hundred.
A decimal can be converted to a percentage by multiplying by one hundred.
Percentage change measures the relative difference between an original value and a new value.
An exponent represents repeated multiplication.
In 2³, the number 2 is the base and 3 is the exponent.
A positive exponent indicates repeated multiplication of the base.
A negative exponent represents the reciprocal of a corresponding positive power.
Any nonzero number raised to the power of zero equals one.
An exponential function has a variable in its exponent.
A logarithm is the inverse operation of exponentiation.
A logarithm answers the question of what exponent is required to produce a particular number.
The common logarithm uses base 10.

The natural logarithm uses the base e.
The number e is an important mathematical constant approximately equal to 2.71828.
An equation states that two expressions have equal values.
A variable represents an unknown or changeable quantity.
A constant represents a fixed value.
An expression is a combination of numbers, variables, and operations.
A coefficient is a number that multiplies a variable.
A term is a component of an algebraic expression separated by addition or subtraction.
A solution to an equation is a value that makes the equation true.
A linear equation has variables raised only to the first power.
A linear equation can often be represented by a straight line.
The slope of a line measures its rate of change.
The y-intercept is the point where a line crosses the y-axis.
The x-intercept is the point where a graph crosses the x-axis.
The slope-intercept form of a line is y = mx + b.
In y = mx + b, m represents the slope and b represents the y-intercept.
Parallel lines have equal slopes when they are not vertical.
Perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is negative one.
A system of equations contains multiple equations involving shared variables.
A system of linear equations can have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Substitution can be used to solve a system of equations.
Elimination can be used to remove a variable from a system of equations.
A system of equations can be represented graphically.
A quadratic equation contains a variable raised to the second power.
A quadratic function produces a parabola when graphed.
The standard form of a quadratic equation is ax² + bx + c = 0.
The quadratic formula can be used to solve quadratic equations.
The discriminant of a quadratic equation is b² - 4ac.
A positive discriminant indicates two distinct real solutions.
A zero discriminant indicates one repeated real solution.
A negative discriminant indicates two complex conjugate solutions.
A polynomial is an expression consisting of variables and coefficients combined using nonnegative integer powers.
The degree of a polynomial is the highest exponent of its variable.
A monomial contains one term.
A binomial contains two terms.
A trinomial contains three terms.
Polynomial multiplication uses the distributive property.
Factoring rewrites an expression as a product of simpler expressions.
The distributive property states that a(b + c) = ab + ac.
The associative property states that the grouping of addition or multiplication can change without changing the result.
The commutative property states that the order of addition or multiplication can change without changing the result.
Addition and multiplication are commutative operations.
Subtraction and division are not generally commutative operations.
An inequality compares two quantities using symbols such as greater than or less than.
The symbol > means greater than.
The symbol < means less than.
The symbol ≥ means greater than or equal to.
The symbol ≤ means less than or equal to.
Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
A coordinate plane uses two perpendicular number lines.
The horizontal axis is called the x-axis.
The vertical axis is called the y-axis.
The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis intersect.
The coordinates of the origin are (0, 0).
A point in a coordinate plane is represented by an ordered pair.
The four regions of a coordinate plane are called quadrants.
The distance between two points can be calculated using the distance formula.
The midpoint of a line segment is the point exactly halfway between its endpoints.
The distance formula is derived from the Pythagorean theorem.
The slope between two points measures vertical change divided by horizontal change.
A geometric point represents an exact location.
A line extends infinitely in two directions.
A line segment has two endpoints.
A ray has one endpoint and extends infinitely in one direction.
An angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint.
The common endpoint of an angle is called its vertex.
Angles are commonly measured in degrees or radians.
An acute angle measures less than 90 degrees.
A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.
An obtuse angle measures more than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees.
A straight angle measures 180 degrees.
A reflex angle measures more than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees.
Angles around a point add to 360 degrees.
Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees.
A triangle has three sides and three interior angles.
The interior angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles.
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides.
A scalene triangle has three different side lengths.
A right triangle contains one right angle.
The Pythagorean theorem applies to right triangles.
The Pythagorean theorem states that a² + b² = c² for a right triangle.
The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle.
The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle.
A quadrilateral has four sides.
A square has four equal sides and four right angles.
A rectangle has four right angles.
A rhombus has four equal sides.
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel opposite sides.
A trapezoid has at least one pair of parallel sides under common definitions.
A kite has two pairs of adjacent sides with equal lengths.
A polygon is a closed two-dimensional shape made from line segments.
A regular polygon has equal side lengths and equal interior angles.
The sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n - 2) × 180 degrees.
A pentagon has five sides.
A hexagon has six sides.
A heptagon has seven sides.
An octagon has eight sides.
A nonagon has nine sides.
A decagon has ten sides.
The perimeter of a polygon is the total length around its boundary.
The area of a rectangle is length multiplied by width.
The area of a triangle is one-half times base times height.
The area of a parallelogram is base multiplied by height.
The area of a trapezoid is one-half times the sum of the parallel sides multiplied by the height.
The circumference of a circle is the distance around the circle.
The area of a circle is πr².
The circumference of a circle is 2πr.
A circle is the set of points in a plane that are a fixed distance from a central point.
The radius is the distance from the center of a circle to its edge.
The diameter passes through the center and has twice the length of the radius.
A chord is a line segment whose endpoints lie on a circle.
A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point.
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
Pi is an irrational number approximately equal to 3.14159.
A three-dimensional solid has length, width, and height.
The volume of a rectangular prism is length multiplied by width multiplied by height.
The volume of a cylinder is πr²h.
The volume of a sphere is 4πr³ divided by 3.
The surface area of a three-dimensional object measures the total area of its outer surfaces.
A cube has six congruent square faces.
Similarity describes shapes that have the same form but not necessarily the same size.
Congruent shapes have the same size and shape.
Similar triangles have corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides proportional.
A scale factor describes the ratio between corresponding dimensions of similar figures.
Trigonometry studies relationships between angles and side lengths.
The sine of an angle in a right triangle is opposite divided by hypotenuse.
The cosine of an angle in a right triangle is adjacent divided by hypotenuse.
The tangent of an angle in a right triangle is opposite divided by adjacent.
The mnemonic SOH-CAH-TOA is commonly used to remember the basic trigonometric ratios.
The unit circle is an important tool for understanding trigonometric functions.
A radian is an angle measurement based on the radius of a circle.
One full revolution is 360 degrees or 2π radians.
180 degrees is equal to π radians.
90 degrees is equal to π/2 radians.
A vector has both magnitude and direction.
A scalar has magnitude but no direction.
Vectors can be added component by component.
The magnitude of a two-dimensional vector can be found using the Pythagorean theorem.
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers or other mathematical objects.
Matrices can represent systems of equations and linear transformations.
Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative.
A function assigns each input in its domain to exactly one output.
The domain is the set of allowed input values.
The range is the set of resulting output values.
A function can be represented using an equation, table, graph, or mapping.
A one-to-one function maps different inputs to different outputs.
An inverse function reverses the input-output relationship of a function.
A sequence is an ordered list of numbers or other mathematical objects.
An arithmetic sequence has a constant difference between consecutive terms.
A geometric sequence has a constant ratio between consecutive terms.
A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence.
The Fibonacci sequence begins with 0 and 1 and each subsequent term is the sum of the previous two terms.
The Fibonacci sequence appears in many mathematical and natural patterns.
A factorial is the product of all positive integers up to a given positive integer.
Five factorial is written as 5!
and equals 120.
Factorials are frequently used in combinatorics and probability.
A permutation is an arrangement where order matters.
A combination is a selection where order does not matter.
Probability measures how likely an event is to occur.
Probability values range from zero to one.
A probability of zero represents an impossible event.
A probability of one represents a certain event.
The probability of an event can be expressed as a fraction, decimal, or percentage.
For equally likely outcomes, probability can be calculated as favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes.
The complement of an event consists of outcomes in which the event does not occur.
Independent events do not affect the probability of one another.
Dependent events affect the probability of subsequent events.
Conditional probability measures the probability of an event given that another event has occurred.
A sample space contains all possible outcomes of an experiment.
An event is a set of outcomes within a sample space.
Statistics is used to summarize and analyze data.
A population is the entire group being studied.
A sample is a subset of a population.
The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.
The median is the middle value when data are ordered.
The mode is the most frequently occurring value.
The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values.
An outlier is an observation that is unusually distant from other observations.
Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean.
Standard deviation measures the typical spread of data around the mean.
A normal distribution is a symmetric probability distribution with a characteristic bell-shaped curve.
The mean, median, and mode are equal in a perfectly symmetric normal distribution.
Correlation measures the strength and direction of a relationship between variables.
Correlation does not by itself establish causation.
Calculus is divided broadly into differential calculus and integral calculus.
A derivative measures instantaneous rate of change.
The derivative can represent the slope of a curve at a point.
A derivative can describe velocity when position is a function of time.
An integral can represent accumulated quantity.
A definite integral represents accumulated change over an interval.
An indefinite integral represents a family of antiderivatives.
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration.
Limits describe the behavior of a function as its input approaches a particular value.
A limit can exist even when a function is undefined at the point being approached.
Continuity describes functions without certain types of breaks or jumps.
A continuous function can be drawn without lifting the pencil under the usual intuitive interpretation.
A derivative can be used to find local maxima and minima.
A critical point occurs where a derivative is zero or undefined, subject to the function's domain.
Optimization uses mathematics to find maximum or minimum values.
Related rates problems analyze how quantities change in relation to one another.
A differential equation contains an unknown function and one or more of its derivatives.
Differential equations are used to model physical, biological, economic, and engineering systems.
A solution to a differential equation is a function that satisfies the equation.
A set is a collection of distinct objects.
The empty set contains no elements.
The union of two sets contains elements belonging to either set.
The intersection of two sets contains elements belonging to both sets.
The complement of a set contains elements outside that set within a specified universal set.
A subset is a set whose elements are all contained in another set.
Mathematical logic uses statements that can be evaluated as true or false.
A proposition is a statement that has a truth value.
A conjunction is true when both component propositions are true.
A disjunction is true when at least one component proposition is true.
A negation reverses the truth value of a proposition.
An implication describes a conditional relationship between propositions.
A proof is a logical argument establishing that a mathematical statement follows from accepted assumptions and previous results.
A theorem is a mathematical statement that has been proven.
A lemma is a proven statement commonly used as part of a larger proof.
A corollary is a result that follows from a theorem or other established result.
An axiom is a foundational statement accepted within a mathematical system.
A conjecture is a mathematical statement believed to be true but not yet proven.
Euclid is often called the father of geometry.
Euclid's Elements became one of the most influential mathematical works in history.
The Pythagorean theorem was known long before Pythagoras, although it is named after him in the Western mathematical tradition.
Archimedes made major contributions to geometry, mechanics, and mathematical physics.
Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz independently developed the foundations of modern calculus.
Leonhard Euler made major contributions to many areas of mathematics.
Carl Friedrich Gauss made major contributions to number theory, algebra, geometry, and statistics.
Ada Lovelace is often associated with some of the earliest published ideas about computer programming.
Alan Turing made major contributions to mathematical logic and theoretical computer science.
Infinity is not an ordinary real number.
Infinity represents an unbounded concept rather than a normal finite quantity.
Some infinite sets can be placed into one-to-one correspondence with proper subsets of themselves.
Georg Cantor developed major parts of modern set theory and the mathematical study of infinity.
The set of real numbers is uncountable.
The set of integers is countably infinite.
A mathematical constant is a fixed value that appears in mathematical contexts.
Pi is approximately 3.141592653589793.
Euler's number e is approximately 2.718281828459045.
The imaginary unit i is defined by i² = -1.
The golden ratio is approximately 1.6180339887.
The golden ratio is commonly represented by the Greek letter phi.
A graph represents relationships between mathematical quantities or objects.
A bar chart displays quantities using rectangular bars.
A line graph displays changes or relationships using connected points.
A scatter plot displays individual observations using points.
A histogram displays the distribution of numerical data using intervals.
A pie chart represents proportions as sectors of a circle.
A coordinate graph can display mathematical functions and equations.
Scientific notation represents very large or very small numbers using powers of ten.
A number written in scientific notation has the form a × 10ⁿ.
Significant figures indicate meaningful digits in a measured quantity.
Rounding reduces the number of digits used to represent a value.
Measurement uncertainty represents limitations in the precision of a measurement.
Dimensional analysis uses units to verify mathematical calculations.
A quantity can be converted between units using conversion factors.
The metric system is based on powers of ten.
The SI system is the internationally recognized system of units.
Length is commonly measured in metres in the SI system.
Mass is commonly measured in kilograms in the SI system.
Time is measured in seconds in the SI system.
Temperature can be measured in kelvins in the SI system.
The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in October 1962.
The Cuban Missile Crisis was a confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union.
The crisis began after the United States discovered Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba.
The Cuban Missile Crisis brought the United States and Soviet Union extremely close to nuclear war.
President John F. Kennedy ordered a naval blockade around Cuba during the crisis.
Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev eventually agreed to remove the Soviet missiles from Cuba.
The United States secretly agreed to remove American Jupiter missiles from Turkey as part of the resolution.
The Cuban Missile Crisis is considered one of the most dangerous moments of the Cold War.
The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki occurred in August 1945.
The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945.
The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Nagasaki on August 9, 1945.
The Hiroshima bombing used a uranium-based atomic bomb called Little Boy.
The Nagasaki bombing used a plutonium-based atomic bomb called Fat Man.
The bombings caused enormous destruction and loss of life.
Japan announced its surrender on August 15, 1945.
Japan formally surrendered on September 2, 1945.
The atomic bombings helped bring World War II to an end in the Pacific.
The bombings marked the first and only wartime use of nuclear weapons against cities.
The bombings began the nuclear age.
The Holocaust was the systematic persecution and mass murder of European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators.
Approximately six million Jews were murdered during the Holocaust.
Millions of other people were also persecuted and murdered by Nazi Germany.
Victims included Roma people, disabled people, Soviet prisoners of war, political opponents, and others.
The Holocaust occurred primarily during World War II.
Nazi concentration camps and extermination camps became symbols of the Holocaust.
Auschwitz-Birkenau became the largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp.
The Holocaust remains one of the most extensively documented genocides in history.
World War I began in 1914.

The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in Sarajevo contributed directly to the outbreak of World War I.
Franz Ferdinand was assassinated on June 28, 1914.
The assassination was carried out by Gavrilo Princip.
World War I involved many of the world's major powers.
The war introduced large-scale use of machine guns, chemical weapons, tanks, aircraft, and submarines.
World War I ended with the Armistice of November 11, 1918.
Millions of soldiers and civilians died during World War I.
The Treaty of Versailles formally ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers.
